# fresh-reader-refresh-80

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html) in a browser. Everything is local; no server, installation or build is required.

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/84-fresh-reader-refresh-80/index.html
```

The artifact is **one comparison table with 70 reading surfaces**, each pairing page-only decisions learned with post-diff misses/corrections and a rule-4 account. [review.md](review.md) is the same table in Markdown. [evidence.html](evidence.html) supplies the method, exact parent/child witnesses and pinned source receipts. [cold-notes.md](cold-notes.md) preserves recall sealed before the source phase.

## Kind

critique

## Subjects

No new teaching subject assigned. This critiques finished teaching surfaces about `pr-127`, `pr-131`, `pr-148`, and `stack`; page 30 also requires the adjacent #146/#147 comparison. Worktrees were read-only. No Symnav build, test, edit, commit or branch operation was performed.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: a reader reporting what a page taught before seeing its underlying diff, then an editor checking omitted distinctions.
- Box lenses: static package ownership, runtime/process boundaries, authority, lifetime and failure/observation boundaries. A box name is insufficient when its outcome changes.
- Opening style: a labelled lossy procedure sketch followed by the main findings and methodological limits.
- Shape: one long comparison table; all rows form the stopping layer, with source/route receipts below the same claims.
- Navigation: linear table; page/capture/source links; local search, subject filter, and direct-witness filter; return links from receipts. No storage or review actions.
- Trust posture: sealed page-only recall, pinned historical revisions, explicit source-only versus witnessed-descent findings. No correctness verdicts, ranks or completeness certificates. Capturing a page is not counted as reading all of it.
- Persona: one sequential agent reader with accumulating knowledge, not a set of independent humans. Earlier critique exposure is disclosed.
- Representations used: comparison table, short procedure diagram, exact parent/child quotations, numbered pinned source excerpts, machine-readable inventories and hashes. Two retained screenshots show the 52/59 stopping registers; they do not measure comprehension.
- Importance rule: prioritize new authority, failure outcome, default/context distinction, ordering exception, side effect, changed test observation and incorrect absence-of-rationale claims. Preserve declared narrow scope; do not turn every out-of-scope fact into a surprise. Test changes have the same explanatory weight as architecture.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): earlier experiment README entry/subject metadata and rendered teaching pages; narration text for 21; immediate `inputs/pr-127`, `inputs/pr-131`, `inputs/pr-148` diffs/PR metadata; pinned `git show` source and `plans/005/daemon-policy.md` from the allowed stack worktree; read-only worktree instructions; generated #146/#147 diffs. The large patches received inventories and focused body/test checks, not a complete line-by-line audit. No web sources.
- Tech: dependency-free Python for inventories/source receipts and report generation; Markdown/JSON; standalone HTML/CSS with small local filtering JavaScript; Playwright for reading surfaces, selected routes and artifact verification.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): read 01–37, 40, 49's four variants, 50–53's teaching surfaces, 59's archived pair, and 61–79. The compared content is cited, not reused as this artifact's UI or findings without attribution. Page 50 embeds prior critique; opening 57 exposed a report, which was then classified report-only. Other earlier critique reports/reader notes were ignored. Evidence/source viewers and kit scaffolds were not counted as additional lessons. Full accounting is in [the method](evidence.html#reading-protocol-and-limits).

## What I tried

I froze finished handoffs at **2026-09-13 12:12:07 UTC** rather than chase concurrently finishing experiments. The 80 finished experiments resolved to 63 with teaching surfaces, 14 report-only handoffs and three negative results. Main entrances, a video, an alternate opening and pair variants produced 70 table rows. Experiments 80, 82 and 83 were unfinished at that cutoff.

I opened the surfaces before the underlying diffs, read their advertised stopping layers and selected descendants, and sealed recall at **12:25:17 UTC**. A hash verifies that the notes were not retrospectively corrected. The source phase checked the small #127 patch and focused production/test boundaries in the much larger diffs. The table preserves those reading limits per row. It is a broad selective reading, not every control state or a full diff audit.

The initial intention to avoid all earlier critique content failed when 50 embedded it and 57 turned out to be a prior review table. I disclosed that exposure and treated related source checks as corroboration. Matching text across 52 and 59's compact/fuller siblings also made it inappropriate to infer a presentation advantage. The table therefore reports learned decisions and misses, not comparative comprehension results.

The clearest operated rule-4 witnesses are optional host policy in 23 and the standalone-clock/authentication/host-policy additions below 29's decision map. The four 49 roots document selected repairs and remaining omissions without being counted as independent route trials. Source-only checks separately expose earlier worker validation, later completion-error provenance, concrete test-stimulus changes and a recorded export-retirement condition. Rich #127 parents already disclose the cache/release distinctions checked here.

Validation checked all 70 rows against the frozen captures, the unchanged recall seal, source receipt hashes, local links/anchors, the single-table structure and required README headings. The browser opened the report through `file://`, exercised search/subject/witness filters and reset, followed a receipt anchor, and checked the narrow viewport without page overflow or script errors. Results are in [validation.json](validation.json) and [browser-validation.json](browser-validation.json). To regenerate the presentation, run `python3 build-report.py` in this folder; `python3 validate-report.py` checks artifact integrity. These checks do not test Symnav behavior or reader comprehension.

## What I would drop

Independent-reader language for this sequential pass; automated capture volume as a proxy for understanding; a pass/fail completeness score; and treating the video, a narrow model, or a matching-text pair as a complete experiment on comprehension. The initial plan to make this wholly critique-blind was abandoned once that became untrue.

## What I would do next

Use genuinely independent readers on the exact frozen 23/29 original/revised roots, ask outcome/authority questions before descent, and retain the same prompts after source exposure. Expand the source audit only where those answers expose a specific unresolved choice.

## Time spent

About 45 minutes for this reading, focused source pass, writing and verification. Timestamps and the phase seal preserve the actual observation order; this is not a reading-speed measurement.

# critique-refresh-80

## Entry point

Open [critique.md](critique.md) in a Markdown reader. Its opening table states what is missing, what repeats, and what is promising; the following sections develop those findings.

[experiment-ledger.md](experiment-ledger.md) accounts individually for **all 81 finished handoffs, 01–81**, at the [final census](scope-final.json). [inspection-notes.md](inspection-notes.md) records reading limits, operated routes, source checks, and hard-rule distinctions. No page was built.

## Kind

critique

## Subjects

none — the finished experiments are the subjects. Targeted stack-source reads check their explanatory claims; this is not a new Symnav correctness review.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: a cumulative, primed critic examining what the collection now enables a reader to understand and question.
- Box lenses: the experiments' source, package, runtime, reference, and lifetime boundaries; the distinction between an explanatory instrument and its complete decision layer.
- Opening style: three concrete relationships, followed by a complete missing/repeating/promising table.
- Shape: synthesis → specific comparisons and qualifications → individual ledger and inspection receipts.
- Navigation: linear Markdown reading with direct links to artifacts, source witnesses, operation states, and the bounded reading ledger.
- Trust posture: distinguish current observations, independently retrieved source, historical reports, authors' reported checks, and unrun learning proposals. No ranking or correctness verdict.
- Persona: the campaign owner deciding what uncertainty the next experiment should resolve.
- Representations used: comparative tables, relationship mappings, prose where the distinction needs it, and linked screenshots of existing artifacts.
- Importance rule: complete understanding and design judgment first; retain test premises, exact rationale scope, comparison conditions, and the cost of decoding a representation.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): philosophy and playbook; finished experiment handoffs and entries; selected briefs and supporting reports; read-only browser operation; pinned Git objects from the supplied worktrees. The stack PR bundle checks #127's stated release rationale.
- Tech: Markdown, Python, Node, an existing Playwright installation, and system Chrome. No new dependencies or external research.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): **01–81 were read**, with the extent recorded in the ledger. Earlier critiques supplied leads. 81's capture approach, itself adapted from 54, supplied the browser-harness structure; current routes and source claims were checked here. No earlier artifact was modified.

## What I tried

The starting scope contained 01–79 and 81. Experiment 80 finished during the reading, so I added its complete handoff, ten reading records, staged/consolidated snapshots, and selected source readers before freezing the final census. Experiments 82 and 84 remained unfinished at that cutoff.

The critique recognizes that later visuals do explanatory work. It examines 79's distinct recovery loops, 80's class/visibility/package boundaries, and 78's fixed cleanup condition against 64's shared event number. It also identifies the unresolved work: composing complete stack understanding, supporting context-sensitive design judgment, carrying corrections into reused claims, and observing unfamiliar human learning.

I captured 80 HTML entries including companions, saved 50 operated states across 16 artifacts, and independently retrieved three source witnesses. These establish available behavior and specific factual distinctions; they do not establish comprehension. Bulk capture output was too unwieldy, so reading shifted to bounded excerpts and targeted full passages. One mistaken navigation selector was corrected and retained in the record. No page prototype or reader study was attempted.

[verification.json](verification.json) checks this handoff's structure, local links, capture availability, operation counts, and clean supplied worktrees. It does not certify every campaign claim or reproduce the authors' Symnav test runs.

## What I would drop

The bulk DOM captures as a reading interface. They are useful receipts but expose too much at once, including off-camera text. The long ledger earns its place as coverage depth; it should not become the default route through the critique.

## What I would do next

Carry the checked corrections into reused claims, then run one bounded human comparison with equivalent conditions. Use its result to attempt composition across a complete stack front, preserving test and rationale qualifications at the relevant boundary.

## Time spent

About 35 minutes, including broad reading, current browser observations, targeted source checks, and the late addition of experiment 80.

# critique-refresh-70

## Entry point

Open [critique.md](critique.md). It is the complete written critique; no install or server is needed.

[experiment-ledger.md](experiment-ledger.md) accounts for every finished experiment. [inspection-notes.md](inspection-notes.md) records reading depth, operated routes, source witnesses, and limits.

## Kind

critique — Markdown documents with local inspection receipts. No page.

## Subjects

None assigned as a new PR explanation. The subject is all **78 finished handoffs, 01–78**, at **2026-09-13 11:52:58 UTC / 14:52:58 Istanbul**. This includes the interrupted negative results 56, 58, and 60. Experiments 79, 80, and 82 were unfinished at the cutoff; this experiment excludes itself.

Targeted reads of #127 and #148 resolve explanatory claims in the corpus. They are not a new implementation correctness review.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: Critic of teaching artifacts, asking what an unfamiliar reviewer could understand and use to question a design.
- Box lenses: Source/package ownership versus runtime use; retained identity versus changing contents; claim provenance from source through reuse.
- Opening style: State the changed diagnosis first, then a table of what is missing, repeated, and promising.
- Shape: Written synthesis, one ledger row per finished handoff, and separate inspection receipts.
- Navigation: Read the critique linearly or follow local links to a particular experiment, observed state, or source witness.
- Trust posture: Distinguish direct source checks, my browser observations, authors' reported results, and interpretation. Do not convert a route miss into a global omission. Apply recent briefs' explicit narrow scopes.
- Persona: Primed cumulative reader of the whole campaign; no claim to be a fresh reader or a human participant.
- Representations used: Comparison tables, local text captures, selected screenshots, and revision-pinned source excerpts. No new teaching page, generated imagery, or ranking.
- Importance rule: Prioritize whether the representation carries consequential meaning, supports informed judgment, preserves context across depth, and exposes evidence-changing test decisions. Novelty and file counts alone do not establish importance.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): Required philosophy/playbook reading; all finished experiment README contracts and main artifact inspection; prior critiques, selected companion pages, runbook/kit material, and the partial study protocol; recent briefs; targeted Git/source reads through the allowed worktrees. Reading limits are explicit in the inspection notes.
- Tech: Markdown; Python for census and handoff checks; Node, an existing Playwright installation, and local Chrome for read-only browser inspection. Opening the critique requires only a Markdown reader. No network research or new dependencies.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): Read all finished 01–78. Adapted 54's local browser-capture approach; used 49's bounded intervention and 59's correction/ancestor distinctions as methodological precedents. Reused no teaching page implementation. Original experiments and comparison stimuli remain unchanged.

## What I tried

I read philosophy first and the required playbook sections next, then worked through the finished corpus. The reading set expanded to include 77 and 78 as their handoffs arrived. A frozen census keeps later concurrent completions outside this critique.

The principal result is that several recent representations now carry a concrete explanatory relationship. The remaining gaps are composition into a complete stack account, transfer from prediction to reasoned judgment, correction propagation, and observed human learning. The critique includes current correction witnesses for 01, 04, 63, and 77, and an operated comparison-state problem in 64.

I captured 66 primary HTML entries and twelve companions, and operated selected routes in eleven artifacts. Two operator mistakes—holding the wrong control in 69 and stopping before the append barrier in 75—were corrected and documented. Three source checks distinguish wrong statements from overbroad rationale gaps. Browser receipts and [verification.json](verification.json) support mechanical checks; they are not learner results or reruns of the authors' source probes.

I dropped the initial temptation to reuse the old diagnosis that the forms are essentially the same. I also rejected whole-PR completeness accusations against recent briefs that expressly permit narrow lessons. No symnav files or earlier artifacts were modified.

## What I would drop

Another refresh should link this ledger and report changed findings instead of reproducing the same census prose. Most automatically captured screenshots are checking material, not part of the argument. More serial agent recall would add little without a specific new intervention or untested relationship.

## What I would do next

Carry the exact correction distinctions into reused claims, then run one matched-content human prediction-and-reasoning comparison. Use the result to test how one narrow relationship composes into a complete stack front.

## Time spent

About 40 minutes wall-clock, including reading, browser operations, targeted source checks, writing, and handoff verification. No deadline was used to stop the work.

# typographic-morphology

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html) directly; no server, installation, network, or worktree is needed:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/80-typographic-morphology/index.html
```

**A word learns its boundaries** follows `WorkspaceDaemon` through four extractions, its rename to `DaemonProcessCoordinator`, package staging, and physical consolidation. Play the changes, scrub eight source snapshots, or select any word to open its explanation and exact receipts. **Escape** returns focus to that word. The focused specimen also accepts Left/Right, Home, and End. Reduced motion retains every snapshot and disables playback.

The ten open readings below the specimen form the complete stopping layer. They can be read in order or entered independently; the source reader has previous/next and return controls. [The static evidence book](evidence/reading.html) works without JavaScript. The animated page and all its sources also work from `file://`.

## Kind

page — animated, interactive typography

## Subjects

stack: main `b6801ebdd2421d0ca2e4bdd61ec0f04c24ddd73e` → #149 `d07002357d3e9596bfaae910a1ac63b77981620b`.

Narrow scope: the ownership, composition, class visibility, package visibility, and test location of **one process shell**, with its four extracted collaborators. The page shows main, #143, #144, #145, #146, #147, #148, and #149. All 27 PR-boundary snapshots were checked for the shell’s public member declarations and named test-declaration census. This is not an explanation of every decision in the stack; constructor-option changes, admission behavior, transport internals, and other owners’ mechanisms are explicitly outside the study.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: reader of a type specimen; follow how a name catches up with the job it contains.
- Box lenses: static class/module/package ownership and class-public versus package-exported surface. The types are the containers; no runtime-process topology is inferred from their duplication.
- Opening style: a compact typographic trajectory, followed by the original compound word and its four still-embedded domain words. The spatial analogy is marked beside the timeline.
- Shape: one box’s history within a pyramid. Opening proposition → animated specimen and ten complete readings → matching mechanisms, author reasons, and exact source receipts. No factual revelation is gated behind playback.
- Navigation: chronological snapshots and a range scrubber; nonlinear word selection; a ten-reading linear source tour; direct `#step=148` and `#read=copies` addresses; browser Back; Escape/focus restoration; static evidence fallback.
- Trust posture: source-grounded explanation. Stated reasons are checked against supplied PR bodies. Precise name choice and exact test selection remain unexplained. Observed counts are separate from author motives. No verdict, scoring, response collection, or persistence.
- Persona: a teammate who knows Symnav but has not read this process shell’s refactor.
- Representations used: fused and separated domain words, a persistent class-name morpheme, variable-font transformation, duplicate impressions at different package addresses, typographic import joins, class-visibility weight, rationale underlines, source counts, and frozen line-numbered receipts.
- Importance rule: moved responsibility and physical ownership first; misleading uses of “public,” staged versus active copies, rationale gaps, and moved tests remain in the complete reading.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): read-only Git snapshots of the class, its four extracted owners, caller entries, class test suites and helper, the compatibility freeze test, package export entries, and the architecture plan; TypeScript AST extraction; local browser observations. Bundle inputs: `pr.json` bodies and commit messages, and selected class paths in `files.txt` / `diff.patch`. The overview dumps and unrelated subject bundles were not used.
- Tech: Recursive variable font, GSAP/Flip/CSSPlugin, native DOM layout and dialogs, TypeScript’s compiler API, esbuild, isolated Chromium/Playwright. Codex harness; no delegated agents.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): no earlier experiment’s implementation, diagram, or evidence package was reused. Read the required READMEs for **04-textbook-chapter, 23-zoom-canvas, 36-be-weird-a, 37-be-weird-b, and 53-be-weird-53** for complete stopping layers, bounded measurement claims, nonlinear return, and marked analogies. Surveyed representation/attempt fields in **07, 19, 60, 66, 70, 71, 74, 76, 78, and 79** to avoid another package map, contract table, matrix, folded instrument, or runtime replay. Existing unfinished research **inside this assigned folder** was retained and narrowed; its snapshot parser and datasets were reused and independently checked.

## What I tried

The folder already contained a broad research pass: vocabulary/import changes, constructor options, 23 proposed readings, member lineage, and package naming ratios. I kept that material but reduced the public artifact to one ownership story and ten readings. Carrying all the vocabulary and options would have made a decorated inventory rather than a typographic explanation. The previous broad layer remains in [content/entry.mjs](content/entry.mjs); it is not bundled into the page.

The central experiment works: the same domain words move from one fused body into separately named classes. At #148 the entire family acquires a second physical impression; at #149 only the package impression survives. GSAP supplies the layout transitions and Recursive’s `CASL` axis supplies the package letterform change. These are schematic source transitions, not recorded runtime events.

The initial desktop draft had excessive vertical space and a constructor parenthesis that could imply the static projector was constructed there. I reduced the space and separated the class-public signature from the import joins. The initial phone version overflowed its four names; two columns now preserve their spelling and selected method samples. A midpoint screenshot also caught entering name parts crossing the moving `Daemon` word; the new parts now appear after that move. Early screenshots are preserved in [evidence/attempts](evidence/attempts/).

A receipt check corrected “identical bodies”: the #148 class source matches **after normalizing one inline import-type path**, while ordinary imports are also re-addressed. Exact raw files remain available. The static audit also replaced an imprecise text search for class declarations with AST confirmation, so declaration strings inside tests cannot count as additional production classes.

## What I would drop

The numerical constructor/member footer is secondary. It requires prose to explain that declarations and formatting lines are not complexity or exact code-move measures. The empty package lane consumes substantial space in early frames, although it makes the later copy visible. The ten complete readings remain more prose than the main type instrument.

## What I would do next

Give a reader the specimen and a conventional diagram with the same facts. Ask which class copy production uses at #148, whether an extracted private method becomes public, and whether the coordinator is a package export. Compare their explanations without a score or leaderboard.

## Time spent

About 30 minutes in this completion pass, including verification and documentation. An earlier research pass was already present in the assigned folder; its elapsed time was not measured here.

## Visual-variable legend

| Variable | Meaning | Bound / caveat |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Green ink + linear letterform | `apps/cli` source owner | An ownership address, not a process or performance state. |
| Brick ink + casual letterform | `@symnav/daemon` source owner | Recursive `CASL` transitions from 0 to 1 as the copy appears. Color is repeated by an explicit package label. |
| Fused versus spaced domain words | A job inside the shell versus its own extracted class | The four domain words abbreviate jobs. Gaps are categorical, not a coupling metric. Prefixes and suffixes expand to actual class names after extraction. |
| Light / heavy **member samples** | Class-private / class-public declaration | Weight does not imply package export. `deliverCompletion` and `executeAccepted` remain private after extraction; `project` and `replace` are public on their new classes. |
| `⌣` joins and shared rule | Direct imports from the shell to the extracted classes | A constructed typographic ligature, not an OpenType language ligature or a call-frequency measurement. “Joins on/off” isolates this channel. |
| Two complete impressions | Source implementations at CLI and package addresses | At #148 the CLI graph remains active and frozen; unit suites follow the staged package. Not two running processes. |
| Solid / dotted underline | Stated rationale / no specific rationale found | Applied to reading words; the renamed class is dotted. An unadorned reading is a source observation. |
| Order and movement | Selected source snapshots across the stack | Eight snapshots have unequal temporal gaps. Interpolation is illustrative, never runtime simulation. |

Letter size supports reading hierarchy and fit; it is **not** proportional to lines, importance, or responsibility. The letterform, package address, method weight, and explicit text together keep the representation usable without color discrimination.

## Libraries considered and used

- **Used: [GSAP Flip](https://gsap.com/docs/v3/Plugins/Flip/)**, installed version 3.15.0. It captures browser layouts before DOM reparenting and animates to the new word locations. GSAP also owns playback scheduling, cancellation, color, and CSS font-axis interpolation. No custom animation engine, FLIP implementation, camera, graph layout, or routing system was written.
- **Used: [Recursive Sans & Mono](https://www.recursive.design/)** through `@fontsource-variable/recursive` 5.3.0. Its weight, monospace, and casual axes let a word retain identity while changing appearance. The local Latin full-axis WOFF2 and OFL license are shipped in `assets/`; no font CDN is required. Native browser shaping and Flex/Grid perform the layout.
- **Considered: [Motion Canvas](https://motioncanvas.io/docs/)**. Its timeline and code-animation facilities suit a narrated film. Here, selectable source text, independent word inspection, keyboard controls, and responsive reflow favor DOM typography with GSAP. It was not installed or used.
- **Considered: [opentype.js](https://github.com/opentypejs/opentype.js)**, installed 2.0.0 by the earlier research pass. Glyph outlines and ligature access could support contour morphs. I rejected outlined text before implementation because contour interpolation would obscure exact spelling and need a second accessible text representation. It remains a development dependency, but is not imported or bundled.
- **Used for extraction/build:** TypeScript 5.9 and esbuild 0.28.2. The compiler identifies classes, imports, members, and named test declarations. esbuild produces the checked-in self-contained script.
- **Used for verification only:** Playwright with an isolated headless system Chrome. No browser dependency is needed to open the result.

## What the form teaches better or worse

**Better:** extraction is felt as a word ceasing to be crowded. A method can visibly remain light/private even after its domain word separates. Two impressions with the same class name make the #148 staging interval harder to confuse with a completed cutover. The #149 deletion removes an address rather than pretending to remove a running process. Letterform and color make the surviving package ownership perceptible.

**Worse:** typography cannot establish behavior preservation, show runtime order, or explain full collaborator APIs. The import joins carry less directional information than arrows. Identifiers with long suffixes are slow to scan; on phones they need two rows. The complete rationale/test story still needs concise prose and source receipts. No human comprehension study was performed, so these are design observations rather than demonstrated learning gains.

## Evidence and verification

- [145 static/source checks](evidence/verification-static.json) independently re-read all 27 snapshots, verify frozen file bytes and SHA-256 hashes, check public member declarations, reproduce named test-declaration counts, reconcile the 44 removed / 7 added member declarations, check the one surviving implementation of each class and the four package entries, and verify both supplied worktrees remain clean.
- [268 browser checks](evidence/verification-browser.json) cover all eight frames at 320/390/768/1440 widths; copy and extracted-word counts; collisions and page overflow; all ten readers and every excerpt; focus restoration; linear and reverse reading; keyboard and URL navigation; a measured intermediate FLIP position; playback/pause/manual-selection cancellation; reduced motion; direct file opening and local font loading; a mobile source dialog; print generation; and a JavaScript-disabled static fallback. The final pass reported no browser errors or external requests.
- [Variable-font transition receipt](evidence/animation-check.json): the entering package word interpolated `CASL` 0.0001 → 0.3869 → 1 and green → brick. These are browser rendering samples of the illustrative animation, not source or runtime measurements.
- [Screenshots](screenshots/) were inspected, including initial, staged, consolidated, phone, source-reader, and font-transition states. [Print check](evidence/print-check.pdf) is also retained.
- [Source manifest](evidence/source-manifest.json), [published model](data/morphology.json), [27-frame research extraction](data/extract.json), and [test-body comparison](data/test-bodies.json) preserve the measurement basis. Sources in the page identify their exact revision, file, and line range, with offline full-file and optional commit-pinned GitHub links.

The class’s 65 → 82 test count means **named test declarations**, counting a parameterized declaration once. The inventory normalizes the class/suite rename and finds no removed declaration. It does not establish equivalent helpers, end-to-end parity, or a correctness verdict. **No Symnav test suite or daemon runtime was executed in this completion pass.**

## Rebuild and repeat

From this experiment folder:

```sh
npm ci
npm run capture
npm run build
npm run verify
npm run check:browser
```

`capture` uses the retained, pinned research snapshots and read-only Git objects available in `~/projects/symnav`. `verify` independently rereads the source and checks `worktrees/main` and `worktrees/stack-head`. Scripts write only inside this experiment. The browser checker defaults to `/tmp/rich-review-05-browser/node_modules/playwright` and system Chrome; set `MORPHOLOGY_PLAYWRIGHT` and `MORPHOLOGY_CHROME` for other installed locations.

For a full research refresh, the earlier `scripts/extract.mjs`, `scripts/build-data.mjs`, and `scripts/test-bodies.mjs` regenerate their corresponding research files before `capture`. They inspect local remote-tracking refs and check the tip pin. The broad `content/entry.mjs` and exploratory probe scripts are retained as an unfinished earlier approach; they do not supply the published ten-reading content.

The received brief is [brief.md](brief.md). No Symnav source or branch was modified, committed, pushed, or rebased. Queue, index, and campaign completion handling are left to the orchestrator.

README
# failure-domain-pinball

## Entry point

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/79-failure-domain-pinball/index.html
```

[Open the pinball table](index.html). No installation, server, network connection or worktree is needed. Phaser and the frozen evidence are local.

Choose a failure domain and condition, then **Launch request** or **Step**. **Space** plays/pauses; **→** steps when focus is outside a form control. **Try local gate** probes the current flippers without changing the recorded route. Click a bumper or an **Inspect** link for its source. Escape closes the receipt and restores focus. Inspection leaves playback paused. On a phone, **Magnify table** enables native sideways scrolling. Reduced motion defaults to instant steps.

The seven open rules remain readable without JavaScript. A local server is optional: `npm run serve` serves this folder at `http://127.0.0.1:8479`.

## Kind

other: game — source-grounded pinball replay, without points, verdicts or review collection.

## Subjects

**stack**, main `b6801ebdd2421d0ca2e4bdd61ec0f04c24ddd73e` → tip of #149 `d07002357d3e9596bfaae910a1ac63b77981620b`.

Narrow subject: the failure vocabulary and available exits of one already-selected warm request. The relevant decisions run through #133, #134, #142, #147 and the #149 package cutover; #148 supplies migration context. This is not an explanation or correctness audit of all 26 PRs.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: learner operating a request through failure domains; assigned pinball angle.
- Box lenses: static package ownership plus runtime failure/request boundaries. The package contains mechanisms in both caller and daemon processes. The worker is inside the daemon process; the injected host executor is distinguished from its package owner.
- Opening style: marked physical analogy, then the main → tip ownership strip. The first sentence names acceptance as the point that changes the exits.
- Shape: complete stopping layer = opening, machine, compact legend and seven open rules. Source dialogs and recordings deepen those same facts. The headline alone is not the complete layer.
- Navigation: 18 replay conditions grouped by domain; sequential stops and previous/next replay controls; direct bumper and rule jumps; related source receipts; direct replay fragments; source close/return controls. Nothing must be won or unlocked.
- Trust posture: actual-method observations and exact source receipts, with explicit projection limits. Reasons are stated only where supplied; the historical guard/terminal precedence selections and choice of exactly one recovery attempt retain bounded rationale gaps. Policy records do state the purposes of both budgets.
- Persona: teammate familiar with Symnav’s purpose, unfamiliar with its daemon failure handling.
- Representations used: numbered guard bumpers, one request-identity ball, local flippers controlled by retry permission, separate recovery loops, package/process enclosures, an inner worker diamond, an outer terminal classifier, neutral state lamps, a capture readout and frozen source/observation drawers.
- Importance rule: acceptance and duplicate-execution consequences first; distinct vocabularies, recovery ownership and classification precedence next. Evidence and rationale limits remain in the open layer.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): read-only main/tip production code and tests; Git objects for the original #133/#134/#142 authority suites; contributor guides; daemon policy, architecture and relevant functional-spec clauses; a fresh daemon package build; actual compiled-method recordings; four focused existing test suites; source hashes and final worktree status. Bundle used: `pr.json` and relevant `repo-rules.md` material. Precomputed overviews and the full net patch were not used to establish claims.
- Tech: **Phaser 3.90.0**, HTML/CSS/classic JavaScript, Python evidence capture and integrity checks, Node actual-method recorder, **Playwright 1.61.1** with system Google Chrome. System fonts; no generated bitmap assets or audio. Codex harness; no delegated agents.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): no implementation, layout, recording or evidence bank reused. Read the required **04-textbook-chapter**, **23-zoom-canvas**, **36-be-weird-a**, **37-be-weird-b** and **53-be-weird-53** READMEs. Surveyed declared representations/attempts from **22-game-any**, **63-daemon-constellation**, **64-lifecycle-music-box**, **65-decision-tetris**, **66-boundary-subway**, **67-blast-radius-terrain**, **72-admission-circuit-board**, **73-daemon-weather-map** and **75-message-particle-chamber**. Borrowed standards of bounded evidence, complete stopping layers, explicit analogy limits and focus-return checks. In particular, 72 already represents admission as a circuit and 75 represents byte/record transfers as particles; this experiment centers the spatial consequences of one identity entering different failure domains, including outer terminal precedence.

## What I tried

Evaluated physics, a rendering stack and a game engine before implementation. Free collisions would allow chance to select a code branch or imply that a stronger launch defeats an admission guard. I chose Phaser’s curves, tween manager and hit areas for controlled replay. Bounce is illustrative; source observations choose the route.

Recorded 18 client cases using real compiled methods with scripted peers, including refusal before submission, each admission refusal, contradictory retry safety, two recovery scopes and their exhaustion, and competing terminal failure facts. The server duplicate bypass and local executor lane remain visibly marked source projections.

The first layout placed controls below a tall board. Browser use led to moving them above it, fitting the board to the viewport and adding native phone magnification. I fixed pending replay timers so changing a case or inspecting a source cannot advance an old run. State now commits when the ball reaches a stop. Initial screenshots remain in [evidence/attempts](evidence/attempts/). No implemented representation was abandoned.

A source audit corrected several initially guessed excerpt ranges, and the policy record refined the rationale wording: budget purposes are stated, while selecting exactly one rather than another bound is not explained. The three direct authority test bodies proved byte-identical from their introductions through tip.

## What I would drop

The chassis screws and serial ornament add little. The miniature phone fit is a locator; reading the board’s labels requires magnification. The seven-rule register is necessary for a complete stopping layer but carries precision that the pinball alone cannot express.

## What I would do next

Give a fresh reader this table and a conventional state diagram. Ask them to explain why a lost socket can recover while a lost worker returns a terminal code, and why result-fetch keeps a capture while reattachment replaces it. No human comprehension trial was run here.

## Time spent

Approximately 45–50 minutes of active work, including source reading, implementation, recordings, browser checks and documentation.

## Visual-variable legend

| Channel | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Amber | Admission vocabulary and the local retry gate. |
| Blue | Transport failures and recovery exchanges. |
| Rose | Outer accepted-execution terminal vocabulary. |
| Lavender | Distinct inner worker-failure domain. |
| Pale cream | Request/result identity; not a “good” verdict. |
| Numbered circular bumper | One admission guard; physical order depicts first-failure order. |
| Package envelope / shaded process regions / dashed seam | Static ownership, runtime containment, and socket crossing respectively. The CLI host shares the caller process but remains outside daemon mechanism ownership. |
| Worker diamond inside worker outline | Injected execution inside a worker thread; its inner vocabulary is not a one-to-one translation to the outer classifier. |
| Brass flippers | Current permission to execute locally, derived from delivery state and authenticated rejection meaning. |
| Return-loop geometry | Reattachment returns to admission and bypasses a new worker execution; result-fetch returns to delivery with the existing capture. |
| Lamps and numeric readouts | Acceptance, manifest receipt, used recovery allowances and capture identity. State only; no score or judgment. |
| Motion | Authored ordering of selected source steps. Speed, distance, force and bounce are invented and have no measured units. |

## Libraries considered and used

| Library | Evaluation |
| --- | --- |
| **Phaser 3.90.0 — used** | Its scene, graphics, input hit areas, curves and tween manager fit one interactive cabinet. Phaser owns interpolation and animation scheduling. The local bundle opens directly without a build. See [Phaser paths](https://docs.phaser.io/api-documentation/class/curves-path) and [tweens](https://docs.phaser.io/phaser/concepts/tweens). |
| **Matter.js — considered** | Suitable for body collisions and physical constraints, but free physics would make guard ordering and recovery branch selection look contingent on momentum. No physics engine determines semantic outcomes here. See [Matter.Engine](https://brm.io/matter-js/docs/classes/Engine.html). |
| **PixiJS — considered** | A capable renderer with interaction and a ticker. This cabinet would still need additional orchestration for its replay. Phaser supplied the required game facilities in one dependency. See [PixiJS interaction](https://pixijs.com/8.x/guides/components/events) and [ticker](https://pixijs.com/8.x/guides/components/ticker). |
| **Playwright 1.61.1 — used for checks** | Exercises real browser input, source navigation, replay state, responsive layouts and direct file opening. It is not needed by the reader. |

The game board’s geometry is authored, as a pinball playfield. This is not a hand-written graph-layout or routing engine. Curves and tween timing come from Phaser. The vendored [Phaser license](vendor/PHASER-LICENSE.md) and lockfile preserve the dependency choice.

## What the form teaches better or worse

The strongest physical fact is the closed local exit after acceptance. A reader can push the flippers, see the state remain closed, and follow a recovery loop that retains the identity. The two loops make “new attempt/fresh capture” versus “same attempt/same capture” spatially memorable. Color keeps the same word from being casually treated as the same failure domain.

A conventional diagram is faster for reading the exact classification precedence, the five outer literals, and rationale gaps. Pinball cannot faithfully depict async concurrency, socket timing, full daemon resource recovery or all message exchanges. One ball groups a request and its return/recovery messages. The open rules and source drawers carry the precision that the analogy loses. These are design observations, not measured claims about reader learning.

## Evidence and verification

- [Decision/depth map and evidence limits](evidence/decision-coverage.md): seven-rule coverage, reason-search boundary, actual versus projected execution, and workspace incident disclosure.
- [Recorded observations](evidence/observations.json): 18 real execution-client cases, five admission contexts and six terminal-classifier contexts. Peers, output and failure facts are injected. No daemon process or worker is launched by the recorder.
- [Frozen sources](evidence/sources.json) and [24 receipts](evidence/receipts.json): full captured files with hashes, exact line ranges and revisions. Pinned GitHub links are optional; offline evidence is complete for the authored claims.
- [Focused test output](evidence/focused-tests.txt): **95 tests passed** in admission, failure vocabulary, execution-client and transport-execution suites. This is not a full-stack verification result.
- [Historical test inventory](evidence/test-inventory.json): three direct authority suites retain byte-identical bodies from first `describe` through EOF; imports and relocation are outside that comparison. Other stack tests were not audited for removals.
- [Browser checks](evidence/browser-checks.json): all 18 paths, all 24 reachable receipts, actual Phaser hit areas, gate probing, keyboard controls, pause/resume, inspector interruption, stale-timer cancellation, natural animated completion, five viewport widths, reduced motion and JavaScript-disabled reading. No page errors or runtime network requests in the local-file checks.
- [Static integrity checks](evidence/static-checks.json): source hashes/excerpts, assets, root/source links, expected observation inventory and clean main/tip worktrees.
- [Screenshots](screenshots/): opening, reattachment, fetch, terminal failure, source receipt and phone view. Screenshots were visually inspected.

No Symnav tracked source, branch or commit was changed. A temporary untracked stylesheet was accidentally created in the daemon worktree during a misdirected UI edit, checked to contain only the newly written CSS, and removed immediately; the [incident record](evidence/decision-coverage.md#workspace-incident) describes it. Both worktrees are clean at completion. Index, queue and commit handling are left to the campaign orchestrator.

## Reproduce the evidence

With the supplied worktrees pinned and the daemon package built, run from this folder:

```sh
python3 scripts/capture.py
node scripts/record.mjs
python3 scripts/inventory.py
python3 scripts/verify.py
```

To repeat browser checks, install this folder’s locked dependencies with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, then run `npm run check`. It uses system Google Chrome by default; `PINBALL_BROWSER_CHANNEL` can select another installed Playwright browser channel.

The focused Symnav test command, run from `worktrees/stack-head/packages/daemon`, was:

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run src/daemon-admission.test.ts src/daemon-execution-failure.test.ts src/transport/execution-client.test.ts src/transport/daemon-transport-execution.test.ts
```

The received [brief](brief.md) and campaign harness log are preserved in this folder.

# origami-depth

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html), or run:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/78-origami-depth/index.html
```

No server, installation, network, or worktree is needed to read the finished artifact. Local GSAP files are included. JavaScript enables the folds and source inspector; the complete six-edge explanation remains readable without it.

Choose **Pocket**, **Accordion**, or **Gate**. The slider opens the same sheet for closer reading. In Gate, compare **Base #126** with **Head #127**, then select a recorded cleanup outcome. Each numbered edge unfolds its mechanism and pinned receipts. **Next fold**, **Previous/Next edge**, native keyboard controls, Escape, source-focus return, and URL/browser history support linear and nonlinear reading.

## Kind

page — interactive semantic origami

## Subjects

`pr-127` only, **Scope semantic caches to one turn**. Base `a1e325a5ff979bdfa25babc5554621c8c0f20497` → head `64919bcbcf7fcc8202779b78c5f069b24662bb18`. Six files, +391/−67.

The narrow teaching subject is **lookup lifetime, reusable handles, and release completion**. It is not a complete daemon or query-algorithm walkthrough.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: learner handling one persistent explanatory object.
- Box lenses: source/module ownership plus runtime object and lifecycle ownership. The TypeScript service owns an instance of a class whose implementation moves to core; the project graph is a collaborator, not a new package.
- Opening style: a marked paper analogy and a visible three-owner sheet, under “The handles stay. The turn folds away.” The separate cache-clear and cleanup-completion boundaries are named immediately.
- Shape: complete stopping layer = opening, sheet/legend and six open edge rows; the same edges then gain mechanism and source fidelity. The heading alone is not the complete layer.
- Navigation: three fold axes/presets on the same DOM sheet; continuous unfolding; direct edge jumps; sequential edge reading; exact return focus; shareable fragment and browser history. No comments, verdicts, storage, telemetry, or score.
- Trust posture: frozen source, controlled actual-method recordings, conservative rationale labels, and an explicit gap between the new await contract and the spec's preservation requirement. Tests are evidence, not a correctness verdict.
- Persona: teammate who knows TypeScript but not this cache-lifetime corner.
- Representations used: hinged paper planes; six persistent handle sleeves and detachable lookup leaves; paired old/new promise slips; coupled cleanup/return flaps; ownership-colored source mapping; exposed-edge contracts; focused mechanism strips; recorded promise-state readouts; exact source windows.
- Importance rule: distinct lifetimes first, ownership second, then retained contracts, API changes, rationale gaps and test changes. No fact is unlocked by a gesture.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): pinned base/head backend and service source; core scope and tests; generic project graph and concrete TypeScript cleanup; head contributor guidance and architecture/follow-up specs; successful builds; controlled compiled-method recordings; focused existing tests; Git pins/clean tracked status and browser checks. From the bundle: PR body and six commits, complete diff, file statistics and relevant repo rules. The overview dumps and other subjects were not used.
- Tech: HTML/CSS 3D; GSAP 3.13.0 and Flip; vanilla JavaScript; Python source capture; Node recorder; isolated Chrome through Playwright 1.55.0. Codex harness, no delegated agents.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): read the required **04-textbook-chapter**, **23-zoom-canvas**, **36-be-weird-a**, **37-be-weird-b**, and **53-be-weird-53** READMEs. Borrowed standards for bounded recordings, source receipts, complete top layers and dependable returns. A fresh declaration survey covered 73 earlier READMEs, including the lifecycle music box (64) and hold/release interface (69). Those use scores, sensory resistance, matrices, or independent navigation axes; this artifact uses intersecting physical fold axes and persistent handles. No earlier implementation, recording, coordinates, or evidence bank was copied. [Survey](evidence/novelty-survey.json).

## What I tried

Considered a folding decision tree, but it would repeat disclosure navigation rather than explain lifetimes. Considered a physical origami mesh, but geometric constraints would not add source fidelity. Built a single strip with three owner regions and a perpendicular set of lifecycle flaps.

The first hinge direction hid the flaps behind their backing paper. Reversing the direction fixed visibility; shorter entry leaves kept the handle labels exposed. A GSAP overwrite conflict initially left the ownership wings bent in later presets; property-level overwrite fixed it. Opening now retains the empty old-lookup markers, so increasing reading depth cannot imply cache repopulation. Negative screenshots and notes remain in [attempts](attempts/README.md).

The final rationale audit distinguished the repo's general requirement for behavior tests from commit subjects naming test intent. It also kept “the PR names the await boundary” separate from “its reconciliation with parity is unexplained.”

## What I would drop

The small printing on bent faces is useful mainly on desktop. On a phone the sheet carries shape and ownership while the adjacent readout and complete edge rows carry readable detail. The decorative paper mark in the opening can go. Flip smooths the lower mechanism's changing height, but GSAP's hinge animation does most of the explanatory work.

## What I would do next

Give a reader only the sheet, legend and six edges, then ask whether an old promise can still settle and whether empty caches imply completed release. Compare their explanation with the same content shown as an ordinary sequence diagram. No human comprehension trial was performed here.

## Time spent

About 40 minutes, including source inspection, design, implementation, controlled recordings, browser checks and documentation.

## Visual-variable legend

| Variable | Meaning | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Terracotta paper | TypeScript query/lifecycle methods; base's manually owned Maps | Class/source ownership, not a process or physical memory region |
| Green paper | Core's generic lifetime class at head | The scope object still belongs to the TypeScript service |
| Blue-gray paper | Project-cleanup collaborator | The TS graph extends the core graph; this is not a third package |
| Vertical crease / owner pocket | Juxtaposes the service, lifetime implementation and cleanup collaborator | A semantic fold; no package dependency is newly introduced |
| Horizontal crease / entry leaf | Removes the old cache lookup while leaving the handle sleeve in place | Six drawn lanes show source structure, not measured occupancy |
| Raised entry layer | Old lookup has been detached | Does not cancel, destroy, or garbage-collect a caller-held value |
| Raised backend and cleanup flaps | Pending completion; head attaches the backend return to cleanup | Angles, distances and duration are illustrative; the recorded text is authoritative |
| Solid versus broken await seam | Head's two awaits versus base's unawaited call chain | Shows source control flow, not transport |
| Exposed handle tabs and lower edge | Same reusable handles, with the surviving contract still readable | Folding never creates a new handle |
| Gold P₀ / green P₁ slips | Caller-held old promise settles; the new cache entry remains new | Actual head core recording with deferred settlement, not a daemon workload |
| Six slots D/R/T/I/O/L | Definitions, reference locations, call target, callers, callees, position locations | First five store promises; L stores locations. Drawn contents are illustrative |
| Open-sheet microprint | Additional implementation fidelity on the same facts | Reading depth does not advance cleanup or refill a cache |

The construction is **semantic origami**, not a mechanically realizable folding pattern. Its angles and expanded writing area are layout choices. The analogy limitation appears beside the instrument, and each controlled mechanism records its own scope.

## Libraries considered and used

| Option | Evaluation / choice |
| --- | --- |
| **GSAP 3.13.0 + Flip — used** | GSAP drives all hinge rotations, source-plane depth and paper extension. Flip handles the lower mechanism's layout-height transition. Property-specific interruption lets quick changes settle to the requested shape. Vendored distribution files preserve their original headers. [Official Flip documentation](https://gsap.com/docs/v3/Plugins/Flip/) and [license notice](vendor/NOTICE.md). |
| **Motion / Framer Motion — considered** | Its independent transform animation and React layout support fit this task, but React would add a runtime solely for a small persistent paper object. [Official animation docs](https://motion.dev/docs/animate), [React layout docs](https://motion.dev/docs/react-layout-animations). |
| **Three.js CSS3DRenderer — considered** | It can position HTML in a 3D scene, but this object needs a fixed perspective rather than a camera/render loop. Its documented zoom limitations also add an unnecessary constraint to a reading artifact. Native CSS 3D retains selectable source text and ordinary DOM controls. [Official renderer docs](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/CSS3DRenderer.html). |

There is no custom animation clock, graph layout, diagram router, or semantic zoom engine. Geometry is an authored three-panel paper net; GSAP interpolates its transforms. Native range inputs, dialog, scrolling and focus behavior provide the interaction primitives.

## What the weird form teaches better or worse

**Better:** a handle and its contents cease to look like the same thing. The sleeve survives while its entry leaf moves away. The perpendicular cleanup fold makes it possible to see “old lookup gone” and “caller still waiting” at once. Switching source revision changes the lifetime owner's paper and the return coupling while keeping the six lanes in place. Opening for evidence preserves those identities.

**Worse:** a conventional sequence diagram states the two awaits more directly and wastes less area. Perspective makes labels harder to read, especially on a phone. Paper cannot carry rationale or test-selection gaps reliably, so the six open prose edges remain necessary. It is not an improvement for a reader who only wants exact API signatures.

## Evidence and verification

- [Decision/receipt map](evidence/decision-coverage.md): every authored deeper fact maps to a complete edge; all 15 diff hunks are assigned.
- [Source inventory](evidence/inventory.json): six changed files, +391/−67; original five service tests/helpers byte-identical; six service and four core cases added.
- [Frozen source bank](evidence/sources.json): 17 documents with revisions and SHA-256 hashes. Receipt windows show original line numbers and can expand to full local context.
- [Controlled recordings](evidence/recordings.json): actual compiled base/head backend calls with an injected empty state and held/rejecting cleanup; actual head core calls with six synthetic handles and a deferred promise. Base fulfills while cleanup is held; head remains pending and carries the same injected rejection. Both clear before cleanup. These are not daemon traces or end-to-end parity evidence.
- Focused existing tests: [5 base service tests](evidence/base-service-tests.log), [11 head service tests](evidence/head-service-tests.log), and [4 head core tests](evidence/head-core-tests.log) passed. [Base](evidence/build-base.log) and [head](evidence/build-head.log) builds passed. No broad Symnav test, lint or parity claim is made.
- [Browser checks](evidence/browser-checks.json): all fold/revision/outcome states; same handle objects and invariant surface text; slider fidelity; all mechanism/source paths; keyboard, history and focus return; interruption and reduced motion; 320/390/768/1440 px layouts; direct file opening, no-JavaScript surface and print. Zero page errors and zero external runtime requests.
- [Screenshots](screenshots/): desktop owner/lifetime/release folds, base comparison, open sheet, mechanism, source and phone. They were visually inspected; draft failures are retained separately.
- [Final folder checks](evidence/final-checks.json): local links, README/brief contract, JavaScript syntax, all frozen source hashes, pinned revisions and clean tracked worktrees.

Only this experiment folder and permitted worktree build output were written. Both Symnav worktrees retain clean tracked status. Source and branches were not modified, committed, pushed, or rebased. Index, queue and campaign completion handling remain with the orchestrator.

## Reproduction

Opening the artifact requires none of these steps. To refresh evidence with the supplied worktrees still at their pinned commits and built, run inside this folder:

```sh
python3 scripts/capture.py
node scripts/record.mjs
```

To repeat browser checks with Node, system Chrome and the pinned development dependencies:

```sh
npm ci
npm run serve
```

In a second terminal in the same folder:

```sh
npm run check
```

`ORIGAMI_URL` can select a different local server address. The capture/record scripts write only this experiment. They do not rerun Symnav's tests. The received [brief](brief.md), original harness/log files, implementation, negative drafts, local runtime files and validation scripts are retained.

# forensic-light-table

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html) directly:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/77-forensic-light-table/index.html
```

No installation, server, network connection or live worktree is needed to read it. JavaScript must be enabled. The renderer and frozen evidence are local.

Choose a spectral film, change its exposure, then drag its colored edge across the plate. The range below the plate provides the same operation by keyboard. **Register all films** restores alignment. Four guided exposures introduce the repeated production bodies, active CLI graph, moved tests and rationale gaps. Select a band or use **Locate a file**; **Inspect source** opens its exact comparison. The nine open readings below the plate are the complete stopping layer, with matching source receipts and return controls.

## Kind

page — interactive canvas light table

## Subjects

pr-148 only: **Own daemon mechanisms behind DaemonClient**. Base `ba53c8e1662fd86d198b95321c90d9c9bef10184` → head `20838f8dbf413e04767543eb2380d0d114da6c60`.

The narrow subject is **the difference between source relocation, source duplication and active mechanism ownership**. This is not an explanation of the entire daemon stack or every execution branch.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: forensic reader comparing registered source specimens.
- Box lenses: static package/module ownership; active consumer graph versus staged public/private surface. The three columns are base CLI, retained head CLI, and new head package files. Separate process and worker entries appear as source owners, not additional invented processes.
- Opening style: a marked light-table analogy and a before/head/head picture: “Same mechanisms. A second owner.”
- Shape: pyramid. Opening, plate, legend and nine open readings form the complete stopping layer. Selected-file comparisons and per-reading receipts deepen the same subjects. The headline alone is not the complete layer.
- Navigation: independent spectral exposures on a registered plate; two specimen sets; four guided exposures; direct file selection and previous/next; linear reading register; next-reading control; locate-on-plate jumps; URL fragments and browser history; dialogs restore focus.
- Trust posture: source-grounded structural explanation. Stated reasons and specific unexplained choices remain distinct. Text matches, direct test imports, a compatibility digest and static reachability each have different meanings. None becomes a correctness verdict or coverage percentage.
- Persona: a teammate who knows TypeScript and symnav but did not write this large PR.
- Representations used: three registered source strips; line-proportional file bands; optical screen compositing; sliding clipping planes; ownership rims; active rails; compatibility dashes; rename arrows; test-import dots; rationale hatching; source comparisons and pinned receipts. No runtime simulation or generated asset.
- Importance rule: distinguish active use from ownership first, then expose residual changes and losses in test evidence. Keep configuration and missing reasons on the complete layer even when those files are outside the imaged specimen sets.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): supplied base/head source trees; TypeScript ASTs; local Git pins and rename inventory; manifest, exports, test configuration, architecture/follow-up specifications and contributor rules; focused execution of six existing boundary-test files. From the bundle: PR body and all commit subjects, complete patch and file statistics. Overview dumps were not used.
- Tech: Konva 10.5.0, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Python `difflib`, the worktree’s TypeScript 6.0.3 parser, and isolated Chrome/Playwright. Built with Codex. No subagents were used.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): no implementation, recordings, source bank or visual assets reused. Read the required READMEs for **04-textbook-chapter**, **23-zoom-canvas**, **36-be-weird-a**, **37-be-weird-b** and **53-be-weird-53** for exact evidence, bounded claims, complete outlines and return navigation. Also read 23’s decision inventory as a coverage checklist, then checked the relevant facts against the supplied source. Surveyed the representation/shape declarations of finished **60–76**, including 68’s microscope, 74’s loom and 76’s specimen atlas. This plate compares structural ancestry and independent evidence membership; it does not reuse their identity matrices, semantic zoom, specimen lifecycle or request enactment. [Survey record](evidence/novelty-survey.json).

## What I tried

Initially considered a full-file bitmap under OpenSeadragon and a two-image before/after wipe. Both emphasized visual registration while hiding the crucial third position: the CLI copy that remains at head. I chose three measured source stations and seven independently composited evidence films. The geometry is a measurement plot, so it needs no graph layout or semantic zoom.

An early similarity probe stripped imports with a regular expression. The final capture uses TypeScript AST import ranges and exact retained lines. It deliberately leaves inline import types, re-exports and indentation in the comparison: 28 counterparts match, while ten retain differences. Those ten are not labeled ten behavior changes.

The first screenshot left selected-file evidence below the viewport. I added an in-plate reading and source button. A browser check then caught mismatched moved-test IDs, which had selected a fallback comparison. The IDs were corrected and all 80 selections checked. Visual inspection caught mobile film controls clipped by their grid; they now use two columns on small phones, and the check explicitly measures their bounds. Two overly broad source ranges were corrected. Initial screenshot and failed-check receipts remain under [evidence/iterations](evidence/iterations).

No full representation was abandoned after implementation. The negative design choices are recorded here rather than presented as functioning alternative artifacts.

## What I would drop

Seven exposure controls are a lot to learn, especially on a phone. The four guided exposures earn their place more consistently. The minimum-width plate needs horizontal scrolling on small screens; native selection and direct source inspection are more useful there than the spatial comparison. The full source bank is valuable for audit but much larger than the 40 curated excerpts.

## What I would do next

Give a fresh reader the plate and an ordinary package diagram with identical facts. Ask them which code the CLI still uses, which tests actually moved, and whether copied text means unchanged behavior. Observe their explanations without scoring them.

## Time spent

Approximately 50 minutes, including source capture, library evaluation, implementation, focused tests, browser checks and screenshot inspection. No human comprehension trial was performed.

## Visual-variable legend

| Channel | Factual meaning | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Column position | Base CLI → head CLI → head daemon source | These are source stations, not three simultaneously running systems. |
| Row and family | One file, grouped by its new package directory | Each plate is a defined subset: 43 new production files or 37 moved mechanism tests. |
| Band length | Count of nonblank lines outside import declarations, kept in source order | A minimum hairline preserves tiny/import-only files. Length is not risk or importance. Physical line counts appear in the inspector. |
| Cyan fill | Exact matching retained source lines | Production compares base↔CLI and CLI↔package separately; tests compare base CLI↔package. Import declarations and blank lines are omitted; inline imports/re-exports remain. Equality is textual, not semantic. |
| Pale dotted arrow | Git-detected path movement | On the production plate this marks the coordinator rename within CLI. On the test plate it spans the empty CLI station for 37 moves. Rename similarity is not coverage. |
| Magenta rim | A newly added source owner in the package | New ownership can surround copied text. A new source file can wrap inherited behavior. |
| Amber rail | Relative value-import/export and literal entry-URL reachability from `apps/cli/src/cli.ts` | This is a static graph, not an executed request. It does not traverse package aliases or evaluate arbitrary dynamic import expressions. |
| Dashed retained-CLI enclosure/underline | Membership in the 38-file compatibility inventory | Compatibility-only describes ownership during staging. Those files can remain active. The digest freezes head source, not equality with base. |
| Green dots | A test source directly imports the production file, including type imports | The inventory covers inspected CLI/package test sources. Blank does not mean untested. Dots are absent on the moved-test plate and never imply passing tests or line coverage. |
| Violet hatching | The file participates in a named rationale gap | Authored association, not a computed amount of unexplained code. Gaps in metadata/lint/runner files remain in open readings 01, 07 and 09 outside the plate’s specimen sets. |
| Exposure and sliding film edge | How much of one evidence category the reader sees | Reader-controlled optical visibility only. Neither opacity nor combined color measures confidence, probability or correctness. |

The important compounds are cyan fill inside a magenta rim (**copied text, new source owner**), an amber rail inside a dashed enclosure (**active compatibility graph**), and test dots under violet hatching (**test source exists, rationale remains missing**). Shape and texture preserve distinctions when colors overlap.

## Libraries considered and used

| Option | Evaluation |
| --- | --- |
| [Konva](https://konvajs.org/docs/styling/Blend_Mode.html) — **used, 10.5.0** | Provides the canvas scene graph, pointer hit testing, drag bounds, [group clipping](https://konvajs.org/docs/clipping/Clipping_Regions.html) and blend modes. All seven films screen-composite in one canvas. Vendored with its MIT license; no CDN requests. |
| [OpenSeadragon](https://openseadragon.github.io/) | Evaluated for registered high-resolution images and multi-image controls. Useful for raster specimens and deep zoom; this source census benefits from selectable vector bands with meaningful per-file identities. Preparing tiled images would add machinery without helping this question. |
| [Image Comparison Slider](https://img-comparison-slider.sneas.io/) | Evaluated for an accessible before/after wipe. A two-image comparison cannot on its own carry retained CLI, package addition and seven independent evidence categories. Native range inputs provide keyboard access to Konva’s actual clipping planes. |
| [PixiJS](https://pixijs.com/8.x/guides/components/scene-objects/graphics/graphics-fill) | Considered for GPU rendering and styled graphics. The bounded 80-specimen corpus does not need a GPU scene or custom shader pipeline; Konva supplies the particular clipping and drag operations used here. |

No graph routing, semantic zoom or animation engine was recreated. Family positions and line scales are explicit measured plot coordinates. The light table has no autonomous animation.

## What this form teaches better and worse

The repeated silhouette makes a huge addition readable as **a second location for existing mechanisms**, while its retained middle column prevents the mistaken conclusion that production use moved too. The test plate’s empty middle column makes an actual move visibly different from a copy. Independent films let a reader see that ownership, activity, test-source presence and rationale can coexist instead of being exclusive node colors.

A conventional package diagram would explain a single call chain faster. This plate makes small client files look physically small even though their boundary is consequential, and source length cannot tell a reader how difficult a change is. The nine open readings carry reasons, deferred behavior and deleted assertions that optical membership alone cannot express. Dense source bands also require selection to identify individual files. Those are real limits of the form.

## Measurements and evidence

The reproducible census finds:

- 153 changed files, +14,624/−815 lines in the supplied patch.
- 43 new daemon production `.ts` files containing 10,666 physical lines.
- 38 explicit CLI counterparts, exactly the set frozen by the PR’s compatibility test; all remain at head.
- 28 counterparts identical after removing import declarations and blank lines; ten have residual text differences.
- 36 of the 38 retained files reachable in the bounded CLI value/entry graph. The other two are contracts consumed through types.
- 37 Git-detected mechanism-test moves from CLI source into package source, with all old paths absent at head.
- Zero whole-word `DaemonClient` mentions in head CLI production source. Existing public-root exposure is different from constructing the facade.

[data.js](data.js) contains all specimens, exact source comparisons, the graph’s predecessor receipts and 221 frozen documents (220 worktree sources plus the supplied PR body/commit-subject record). [inventory.json](evidence/inventory.json) records every pairing and move. [diff.patch](evidence/diff.patch) preserves the original 153-file patch. The table measures source structure; it does not run symnav or model time, network behavior, output bytes or coverage.

Reasons were searched in the supplied PR body and commit subjects, pinned architecture specification and changed follow-up specification. Test names and commit subjects establish intent; they are not automatically treated as explanations. The complete readings retain the gaps in digest choice, lifecycle details, coordinate/authentication specifics, policy-testing removal, worker test promises, runner settings and Windows cleanup expectation.

## Validation

[Static checks](evidence/static-checks.json) verify all 80 unique specimens, all nine reading targets, all 40 receipt ranges and exact hashes/text for 220 worktree sources. Both worktree pins are checked and both remain free of tracked modifications.

[Browser checks](evidence/browser-checks.json) passed in isolated system Chrome through Playwright. They cover actual pixel changes for all seven exposure and clipping controls, pointer dragging, native keyboard operation, every specimen selection, every curated receipt, all four guided exposures, dialog focus/Escape, next/previous navigation, deep links/history, direct `file://` opening, reduced motion, printing and 1440/768/390/320 px layouts. There are no browser errors or external requests. The plate intentionally scrolls within its own container on narrow screens; the surrounding page and all film controls fit.

Six existing head test files were run: **26 tests passed**. [Meta-test output](evidence/meta-tests.log) records eight checks of package metadata and the 38-file freeze. [Package-test output](evidence/package-tests.log) records 18 host/declaration, executable-entry, package-boundary and public-facade checks. These do not establish end-to-end parity; no full suite or Windows process run is claimed. The optical test dots continue to mean direct test-source imports, independently of this focused run.

Final screenshots in [screenshots](screenshots) were visually inspected for the opening, partial film, active graph, moved tests and phone layouts. The mobile-control clipping discovered by inspection was added to automated bounds checks. The artifact stores no review comments, verdicts, scores or user responses.

## Regeneration

Reading the artifact requires none of these commands. With the supplied pinned worktrees and their installed TypeScript still available:

```sh
cd ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/77-forensic-light-table
npm run capture
node scripts/verify.cjs
```

`capture` reads only the supplied inputs/worktrees and writes this experiment’s evidence. To rerun browser checks, start `npm run serve` in another terminal and run `npm run check`. Set `LIGHT_TABLE_PLAYWRIGHT` to an installed Playwright package path if `/tmp/rich-review-05-browser/node_modules/playwright` is unavailable. Checks use installed Google Chrome. The pinned renderer can be restored with `npm ci`; reading uses the already-vendored copy and needs no install.

The received brief is preserved in [brief.md](brief.md). Index, queue and commit handling are left to the orchestrator.
