README
# scientific-specimen-atlas

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html) directly, offline:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/76-scientific-specimen-atlas/index.html
```

**What survives a fresh start?** compares two prepared specimens. Follow sections 01–03, use the selective stain to isolate a lifetime class, then change an intervention in the recorded experiment. Each of the ten findings links to its structure notes and returns to the same finding. Source receipts open locally; Escape closes them and restores focus. Prediction answers reveal locally. Nothing is stored.

No install, server, network or live worktree is needed to read the page. On narrow screens the three sections stack vertically. JavaScript enables the figures and experiment controls; the complete finding register, structure notes, prediction answers and [source book](evidence.html) remain readable without it.

## Kind

page

## Subjects

pr-127 and pr-131. The narrow subject is **selective reset: which state survives a lifetime boundary?** This is not a whole-PR explanation or decision census. In #127 it follows cache handles, entries and caller-held promises. In #131 it follows the required delivery slice, per-attempt fetch state and outer reattachment state. Other policy consumers, timing purposes, resource thresholds and daemon mechanisms are outside this specimen.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: learner reading a comparative scientific atlas, with a controlled intervention and a prediction after the overview.
- Box lenses: static ownership (core implementation / TypeScript instance; daemon policy / CLI consumer) and lifecycle ownership (persistent enclosure, resettable contents, caller-held value). No process migration is implied.
- Opening style: picture and a marked prepared-section analogy. The same structures are registered at three discrete checkpoints.
- Shape: pyramid. The overview plus the ten open findings are the complete stopping layer. The laboratory, structure notes and source receipts add fidelity to those findings.
- Navigation: linear reading with direct finding → structure → source exits; per-finding return anchors; native browser history; keyboard-accessible experiment tabs and selects; local prediction disclosures. No semantic zoom or free camera.
- Trust posture: compare stated reasons with actual source and controlled execution. Specific rationale gaps remain in the opening register, including awaited release, larger fetch allowances, error provenance and exact test selection. No correctness verdict.
- Persona: a teammate who knows the project but not these lifecycle implementations.
- Representations used: paired serial sections; repeated faceted owner enclosures; stable handle cells; value and counter glyphs; selective lifetime staining; measured search-count plots; measured wire-count plots; before/head result tables; predict/reveal; pinned source receipts.
- Importance rule: reset boundaries first, then what survives them, caller-visible differences, and limits of the evidence. File count does not determine diagram area.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): the four supplied base/head worktrees and their compiled modules; architecture spec at both heads; #131 policy rationale record; relevant follow-up-spec searches; source tests and test adapter; Git pins and clean tracked status; controlled recordings and focused head test execution. Bundles used: both PR bodies and commit messages, file inventories and patches; relevant repo-rules searches. The precomputed symbol overviews were not used.
- Tech: Observable Plot 0.6.17, Tufte CSS 1.8.0 with local et-book fonts, native HTML/CSS/JavaScript, esbuild 0.25.10, Python source capture, Node recording, Playwright 1.61.1 and system Chrome. All reading assets are local. Codex harness; no delegated agents.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): read the required 04-textbook-chapter, 23-zoom-canvas, 36-be-weird-a, 37-be-weird-b and 53-be-weird-53 READMEs. Borrowed their standard of bounded recordings, pinned receipts, explicit analogy limits and reliable returns. Surveyed representation declarations in 60–73 and read further portions of 62-policy-stained-glass, 64-lifecycle-music-box, 68-semantic-zoom-microscope and 70-bauhaus-daemon-grammar. No earlier implementation, coordinates, evidence bank or recording was reused. Existing brief/harness/worker-log files in this folder were preserved.

## What I tried

I considered a lifetime timeline and a policy-capture atlas, then chose serial sections of **nested scope** so the small and wide PR share a visual grammar. This avoids repeating the identity matrix in 36, orthogonal navigation in 37, release spring in 53, microscope camera in 68 or policy distribution figure in 62.

The first render used marks that were too small and three horizontal sections on phones. Screenshots led to larger glyphs and labels, rounded owner enclosures, real dashed reset boundaries, and vertically faceted phone sections. A cleared-but-not-yet-queried cache checkpoint initially looked like a replacement entry; the recorder now verifies zero entries there and the chart uses an open mark. Release tables now show the pending checkpoint as well as settlement.

The custom fetch-allowance experiment is a useful negative result: allowance three produces **one fetch**, then `corrupt`, when the resumed stream ends incomplete. The first fetch has no repeated-fetch loop on that path. A separate recording preserves the later-error difference between base and head. No complete representation was abandoned. The initial recorder used the wrong symbol-identity shape; it was corrected before any displayed observations were captured.

## What I would drop

Some repeated owner labels in the serial sections could shrink for an expert audience. The prose structure notes are longer than the visual plate; error selection earns that space, but the ownership explanation partly repeats what the plate already shows. The phone layout trades horizontal comparison for a substantially longer page.

## What I would do next

Give readers the plate alone and ask them to predict which handle, promise and counter survives each boundary. Compare their explanations with those elicited by a conventional before/after diagram; no human comprehension trial has been performed.

## Time spent

Approximately 30 minutes for this implementation, including required reading, recordings, source reconciliation, browser inspection and documentation. Earlier harness attempts are preserved separately and are not included in that estimate.

## Visual-variable legend

| Variable | Meaning | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Teal / rust on the plate | Original or retained scope / contents belonging to a newly begun scope | Pigment is a lifetime class, not a memory address or object identity across builds. |
| Enclosure and nesting | Who holds the state; inner dashed enclosure marks the reset scope | Geometry is a prepared-section analogy, not physical memory or a biological measurement. |
| Rectangle / circle / diamond | Reusable structure / value or promise / counter | The output glyph groups receiver and output for the attempted transfer; the label names output. |
| Position outside the cache scope | The caller still holds the old promise | It does not imply a different process or a garbage-collection measurement. |
| Repeated section position | The same role at the next observation checkpoint | Spacing is not elapsed time; section count is not a retry budget. |
| Selective stain | Isolate retained, fresh or outside state without hiding the findings | This is an inspection control, not live execution. |
| Cache laboratory y-position | Number of definition searches actually started | Empty controlled workspace; no duration or semantic answer quality is measured. |
| Filled teal / rust / open cache point | Original entry / replacement entry / cleared and still empty | Handles are checked independently; a new entry is not a new handle. |
| Delivery laboratory x-position and shape | Recorded execute/fetch request counts; square = execute, diamond = fetch | Teal/base and rust/head are explicitly relabeled for this chart. Execute requests are not proof of command reruns. |

The six cache abbreviations and both counter denominators are decoded beside the figures. No quantity is encoded in enclosure size.

## Libraries considered and used

| Library / system | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| [Observable Plot](https://observablehq.com/plot/) | Used for shared scales, repeated facets, SVG marks, text and measured plots. It lays out the comparison panels and their axes; authored coordinates encode semantic containment rather than graph routing. |
| [Tufte CSS](https://edwardtufte.github.io/tufte-css/) | Used for et-book typography and publication figure conventions, with a local responsive atlas stylesheet. Font files and licenses are included. |
| [Vega-Lite](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/docs/facet.html) | Evaluated through its official faceting documentation. Capable of the same repeated-view structure, but its runtime and declarative selection model add little for these few ordinary DOM controls. |
| Quarto | Considered as a notebook/report shell. No kernel, notebook dependency or report server is needed for saved observations and local source excerpts. |
| Handwritten graph layout / zoom / animation | Not used. This is a faceted specimen field, not a routed node graph or camera; Plot handles the relevant layout. |

## What the form teaches better or worse

The prepared sections let the eye follow **one retained enclosure and one replaced interior at the same time**. Registering the two specimens makes the shared principle visible: a new inner scope does not reset its enclosing lifetime. The outside promise also makes “cleared” visibly different from “cancelled.” Staining gives the reader a way to inspect that distinction without switching to a different diagram.

A conventional before/after diagram would show the package move more economically. It would also be easier to scan on a phone. Serial sections do not naturally show which error escapes a nested `try/catch`, so that finding uses a recorded comparison and a short source explanation. The atlas does not prove that this visual grammar improves understanding; that remains a reader study.

## Evidence and verification

- [Source capture](evidence/sources.json): 15 frozen documents, 20 selected receipts and four revision pins. Worktree bytes are checked against their pinned Git objects; document hashes and line ranges are preserved. Both supplied PR bodies and all their commit messages are captured.
- [Raw observations](evidence/observations.json): ten cache scenarios across base/head; eight scripted local-socket runs; four isolated outer-completion probes; three factory outcomes. The browser selects recordings rather than executing or simulating arbitrary cases.
- [#127 focused head tests](evidence/tests-127-head.txt): **15 passed** across the core scope and semantic service suites. The five original service tests and helpers are byte-identical to base; six service and four core cases are added.
- [#131 focused head tests](evidence/tests-131-head.txt): **35 passed** in the existing local-daemon-transport execution suite. The atlas does not claim a full-PR test audit or end-to-end parity. Existing base suites were not rerun.
- [Browser checks](evidence/browser-checks.json): direct file reading, all four stains, all ten finding returns, browser history, all 20 source dialogs, both experiment selectors, keyboard tabs, prediction disclosures, standalone receipts, and no-JavaScript reading. No page errors, external runtime requests or horizontal page overflow at 320/390/768/1440 pixels.
- [Screenshots](screenshots/): the desktop overview, both laboratory views, phone specimen and laboratory, and source dialog were inspected. The selected screenshot is an artifact check, not evidence of Symnav behavior.
- [Pyramid mapping](evidence/pyramid-map.md) and [static checks](evidence/static-checks.json) record scope, sources, internal links and clean tracked worktrees.

All four worktrees successfully ran `pnpm build`; only permitted build output was written there. Symnav source and branches were not changed, committed, pushed or rebased. Queue, index and experiment commit handling remain with the campaign orchestrator.

## Regeneration

Reading the finished page requires none of these commands. To regenerate from the supplied, built worktrees:

```sh
cd ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/76-scientific-specimen-atlas
npm ci
npm run capture
npm run record
npm run build
npm run check
node scripts/verify.mjs
```

The browser checker defaults to system Google Chrome; `ATLAS_CHROME` can select another executable. Capture and recording write only inside this experiment and temporary fixture directories they create themselves. They do not rerun the focused Symnav suites.

# message-particle-chamber

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html) directly, or run:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/75-message-particle-chamber/index.html
```

**Keep the work. Recover the answer.** starts paused at an interrupted result transfer. Choose Frame, Transfer, Identity or Lifetime, then a condition. Play, step or scrub. In **Hold the first append**, release the injected barrier to advance the offset. “Inspect this boundary” opens its source receipt; Escape closes it and restores focus. The seven open facts link into their experiments and have a return link.

No installation, server, network or live worktree is required to read it. WebGL and JavaScript enable the chamber. The complete facts and [source book](sources.html) remain available without JavaScript. Small screens scroll the chamber horizontally inside its own viewport; the controls and state description fit the page.

## Kind

other: interactive simulation

## Subjects

pr-148 only — **Own daemon mechanisms behind DaemonClient**. Base `ba53c8e1662fd86d198b95321c90d9c9bef10184` → head `20838f8dbf413e04767543eb2380d0d114da6c60`.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: learner operating a particle chamber. The narrow lesson is accepted-work identity versus transfer progress versus completion ownership.
- Box lenses: static package ownership and runtime/data ownership. The opening strip distinguishes package staging from the still-active CLI compatibility graph; chamber enclosures distinguish daemon spool, client capture and accepted ledger.
- Opening style: a lossy physical picture of a broken connection with retained particles. The first state already contains two captured records.
- Shape: a complete surface consisting of the opening ownership strip, instrument/legend and seven always-open facts. Optional experiment checkpoints and receipts refine those facts. This surface spans several viewports; the headline alone is not the complete pyramid.
- Navigation: linear playback/stepping and ordinary scrolling, plus direct scene/condition selection, fact-to-experiment links, source dialogs, return links and scene/condition URL fragments.
- Trust posture: source and controlled observations, with stated rationale separated from bounded rationale gaps. The artifact teaches without collecting verdicts, comments or review state.
- Persona: a teammate familiar with symnav but new to resumable daemon delivery.
- Representations used: byte accumulation at a length gate; record particles docking in ordered capture slots; curved fetch and reattachment trails; identity fusion and rejection rebound; diagnostic-halo decay with persistent spool/ledger; source receipts and a compact open decision register.
- Importance rule: replay authority and the distinction between completion owners first; validation, retention, staging and scoped test changes stay on the complete surface.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): read-only base/head source and built classes; relevant architecture/follow-up specifications; compatibility-freeze test; four relocated test pairs; new client capture/composition tests; controlled recordings; builds and focused existing tests. Bundle inputs used: `pr.json` and `files.txt`; scoped source-to-source comparisons supplied the relevant diffs. No other PR worktree, implementing conversation or precomputed symbol overview was used.
- Tech: PixiJS 8.17.0 ParticleContainer/Graphics/Text; GSAP 3.13.0 timelines and MotionPathPlugin; esbuild 0.25.10; Node recordings/source capture; Playwright 1.61.1 with system Chrome; axe-core accessibility checks. Local system fonts. Codex harness; no delegated agents.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): no implementation or evidence reused. Read required READMEs **04-textbook-chapter**, **23-zoom-canvas**, **36-be-weird-a**, **37-be-weird-b**, **53-be-weird-53**, and additionally **15-message-choreography-sim**, **64-lifecycle-music-box**, **66-boundary-subway**, **67-blast-radius-terrain**, **68-semantic-zoom-microscope**, **69-command-me-reader**, **70-bauhaus-daemon-grammar**. Borrowed bounded recording claims, exact receipts, complete surfaces and focus/keyboard standards. Avoided repeating message envelopes, transit routes, identity matrices, orthogonal navigation and a resistance bench. READMEs 72–74 were not present when surveyed.

## What I tried

Considered rigid-body collision physics, then chose deterministic protocol responses: a checksum failure is a predicate, not an elastic force. Every particle encodes a byte, message, record, identity or diagnostic trace; there is no ambient particle field.

The first instrument could explain the append barrier but could not hold it. Added a held-append condition tied to a real promise-gated receiver probe. Browser checks caught an off-by-one visual arrival at the final byte and an unlabeled-role accessibility issue; both were corrected. Screenshot inspection also corrected a lifetime scene that said “await manifest” despite retained records, and a conflicting-identity label that incorrectly suggested the original work had failed. No implemented representation was abandoned. The initial failed browser receipt is retained.

## What I would drop

The repeated empty capture slots in the identity scene add less than its single accepted-entry collision. The large two-process instrument also costs vertical space, and its full geometry requires horizontal scrolling on a phone.

## What I would do next

Ask an unfamiliar reader to predict what survives a disconnect, trace expiry and acknowledgement, then compare with an ordinary sequence diagram. No human comprehension trial was performed here.

## Time spent

Approximately one hour including guidance/source reading, library evaluation, recordings, implementation, verification and screenshot inspection.

## Visual-variable legend

| Variable | Meaning | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Violet circles | Control messages: acceptance, manifest, end | Letter glyphs identify the selected control; not actual serialized shapes |
| Cyan squares / amber triangles | stdout / stderr records | Numeric labels, not color, carry sequence identity |
| Tiny colored dots in Frame | One dot per actual encoded byte: prefix, header, raw payload | Spatial grid is invented; 186-byte fixture is real |
| R7 / T1 / 0…3 | Request, transfer and record identity | Fixed fixture identifiers, not production values |
| Straight outbound / curved return trails | Original delivery / fetch, reattachment or acknowledgement | Direction carries mechanism; lengths and travel times have no protocol meaning |
| Dock, fuse, coral rebound | Append completes, matching ledger entry is reused, or validation rejects | Rebound is never a real response packet; it does not fail the original accepted entry |
| Enclosures and filled slots | Process boundary and ownership of stored records | Grouped module geometry is lossy; the package boundary is shown separately |
| Fading dashed halo | Disconnected diagnostic trace expires | Fade is an analogy for a discrete callback; no gradual spool eviction |
| Empty server spool + retained R7 | Ack cleanup and retained ledger bookkeeping | Normal cleanup succeeds in this recording; source also records cleanup errors |

The compact on-page legend and local analogy notice accompany the instrument. Fixed timing, geometry, illustrative transitions and source-walk checkpoints are explicitly identified.

## Libraries considered and used

Used [PixiJS ParticleContainer](https://pixijs.com/8.x/guides/components/scene-objects/particle-container) to batch byte/trail marks and its scene graph for labels and boundaries. Used [GSAP timelines](https://gsap.com/docs/v3/GSAP/Timeline/) for playback, seeking and interpolated transitions; MotionPathPlugin supplies trajectory interpolation. Versions, notices and licenses are bundled locally.

Considered [Matter.js](https://brm.io/matter-js/docs/classes/Collision.html), but physical momentum would invent scheduling and collision semantics. Considered Three.js and regl: their depth/shader work offered no benefit for this planar ownership lesson. No custom animation clock, physics engine, diagram router or graph layout was implemented.

## What the weird form taught better or worse

Keeping two particles on the client side when the connection disappears makes partial capture tangible. Fetching only the remaining ordinals distinguishes transfer recovery from execution replay. Holding a particle outside its slot while the offset stays fixed expresses the append barrier. Letting only the halo disappear makes the trace/spool/ledger lifetime split visible in a way a single “completed” state obscures.

The form is worse at wire-field syntax, exception taxonomy and rationale. Those need terse text and receipts. A conventional sequence diagram is more compact and requires less legend learning. These are design judgments, not measured comprehension gains.

## Evidence and verification

- [Recorded observations](evidence/observations.json): real compiled base CLI and head package classes; fragmented/coalesced framing, corruption, held append, eight execution-client cases, ledger identity/conflict, retry authority, trace expiry and ack cleanup. All recorded base/head observations match for these fixtures.
- [Recorder](scripts/record.mjs): scripted incoming bytes, injected acknowledgement failure, real in-memory capture/spool, fixed identities/clocks, and a 12 ms trace-retention override. The UI shows the current five-minute policy and marks compressed time. These are neither live daemon/network traces nor performance measurements. One lifetime fetch is a labeled source walk supported separately by the client resume recording.
- [Source receipts](evidence/receipts.json): 24 frozen excerpts/comparisons with revisions, line numbers and full-file hashes where applicable. The page runs authored explanatory transitions over the measured facts; it does not execute symnav in the browser.
- [Test comparison](evidence/test-inventory.json): the four selected test bodies preserve assertions; only imports and the delivery test's fake-clock constructor differ. This is a scoped comparison, not a claim about all tests in the 153-file PR.
- Existing focused tests passed: **44 base tests and 44 head tests**, four files per revision. [Base report](evidence/base-tests.json), [head report](evidence/head-tests.json). Both relevant builds succeeded. New client-composition tests are cited as source, not included in this execution count.
- [Browser checks](evidence/browser-checks.json): **105 checkpoints across 14 conditions**, boundary receipts and focus return, held append, pause/scrub, direct-file opening, responsive layouts, reduced motion and no-JavaScript reading. No page errors, external requests or automated WCAG A/AA violations. [Final focused checks](evidence/final-browser-checks.json) cover the corrected labels, fact return links and larger phone rendering. [Screenshots](screenshots/) were visually inspected.
- [Static checks](evidence/static-checks.json): local links/anchors, source hashes and excerpt equality, required README headings, absence of review storage and clean tracked worktrees. The complete surface-to-mechanism mapping was also inspected manually.

No Symnav source or branch was modified. Index, queue, campaign logs and publishing are left to the campaign. All authored output is in this experiment folder. Rationale search was bounded to the supplied PR/commits and relevant specifications; “unexplained” never claims that no rationale exists elsewhere.

## Regeneration

Reading needs none of these steps. With the pinned worktrees built, run from this folder:

```sh
npm ci
node scripts/record.mjs
node scripts/capture.mjs
npm run build
```

For browser checks, run `npm start`, then `npm run check` in a second terminal. System Google Chrome is required by the checked-in browser script. These scripts write only to this experiment or temporary fixture directories. The received brief and design/attempt notes are retained beside the artifact.

# policy-reading-loom

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html) directly, offline:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/74-policy-reading-loom/index.html
```

No installation, server or live worktree is needed to read it. Select a consumer–slice crossing, then choose **Surface / Wiring / Receipts**. Depth stays fixed when either coordinate changes. **One field 64 KiB**, **Same value 250 ms**, and **Two allowances 1 + 1** pull different sets of strands. The exact-field selector exposes every drawn leaf.

On a focused crossing, arrow keys move through the grid; Page Up/Down changes depth. **Previous / Next** follows the fifteen active crossings. **Return to surface** keeps the crossing. **Locate crossing** restores grid focus. Browser Back restores the address; receipt dialogs close with Escape and return focus. All twelve open readings and the [source book](evidence.html) work without JavaScript. Narrow screens scroll the matrix inside its own viewport and provide ordinary coordinate selectors.

## Kind

page — interactive grid

## Subjects

pr-131 only: **Route daemon thresholds through centralized policy**. Base `b3a6c4fa5dcf96223765aa147a9e094cd4a51b0e` → head `b100221db48754656328391b878299c5a0bab443`. Sixty changed files, +1,298/−544. The preceding policy snapshot is existing context, not attributed to this change.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: a learner comparing policy identity with consumer purpose. Narrow question: **does sharing a field mean sharing a job, and does sharing a number mean sharing a field?**
- Box lenses: static package/module ownership and composition/input authority. Policy lives in `@symnav/daemon`; the named consumer families remain in `apps/cli`. The earlier parent-side worker parse is an explicit runtime failure-boundary exception.
- Opening style: a marked loom analogy and before/after authority strip. Intuition comes from pulling one leaf through several consumers, then pulling equal numbers that do not connect.
- Shape: complete stopping layer = opening + fabric/legend + twelve open readings. The optional inspector repeats the same subjects as wiring and source receipts. Eight readings have stated reasons; four retain specific rationale gaps. A stated general migration reason does not fill a specific implementation gap.
- Navigation: address `(consumer family, policy slice, depth)` plus an independent highlighted thread set. Seven rows × seven columns remain fixed at every depth. Even empty coordinates can be selected. Linear active-crossing traversal, reading-to-crossing jumps, exact returns, URL fragments and history supplement the grid.
- Trust posture: pinned source, conservative reasons, bounded actual-method observations and explicit changes to test premises. No correctness judgment, verdict buttons, comments, review storage or collected responses.
- Persona: a TypeScript-familiar teammate who has not followed daemon policy composition.
- Representations used: orthogonal matrix; individual field strands; shared/unique knots; reading/forwarding ties; rationale rims; three thread comparisons; byte-proportional recorded output bars; open marginal readings; exact line-numbered source dialogs.
- Importance rule: distinguish field identity, purpose and enforcement first. Recovery errors, parent validation, adapter behavior and deleted/changed tests remain on the open surface even when they make no attractive strand.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): pinned head/base implementations and changed test source, unchanged policy implementation and tests, `plans/005/daemon-policy.md`, architecture specification, Git blobs/status, and a fresh probe of actual capture/codec/worker-validator methods. Bundle used: `pr.json` including all six commits, `diff.patch`, `files.txt`, and relevant `repo-rules.md` clauses. Overview dumps and other subjects were not used. No implementing conversation was supplied.
- Tech: D3 7.9.0, HTML/CSS/SVG, esbuild 0.25.10, Python source capture, Node method probe, Playwright 1.61.1 and system Chrome. System fonts; local assets and bundled runtime dependencies. Codex; no subagents.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): **37-be-weird-b** supplied the independent-addressing principle, extended here from decision × depth to family × slice with depth held separately. The required READMEs for **04-textbook-chapter, 23-zoom-canvas, 36-be-weird-a, 37-be-weird-b and 53-be-weird-53** informed pinned receipts, bounded recordings, complete stopping layers and focus returns. No earlier implementation, evidence bank or probe was copied. A README representation-field survey across existing experiments, plus closer reads of **62-policy-stained-glass** and **67-blast-radius-terrain**, avoided glass regions, ranked readership, terrain and shared-file overlap as the explanation. Representation metadata for **61, 65, 66, 68 and 69** was also inspected. The distinction here is a fixed individual-leaf matrix with three independent reading coordinates; it does not count references or project overlaps into geography.

## What I tried

Compared spreadsheet grids, Plot cells and D3 before implementation. A cell containing one aggregate symbol would hide whether two families read the same leaf, so the final fabric draws every one of the 38 traced leaves as its own vertical strand. Fifteen family–slice crossings contain 53 knots. Light ties distinguish forwarding from reading. Empty grid positions remain navigable to preserve the coordinate algebra.

The first browser render exposed a missing favicon; it was fixed. Source reconciliation added the base production entry for the already-hard-RSS reporting claim and the benchmark return shape for the adapter claim. Full-width screenshots made it clear that the whole grid needs its own reading viewport below the large opening. On phones, the grid remains horizontally scrollable while the inspector uses normal text and selectors. Draft captures are retained under [evidence/attempts](evidence/attempts/). No complete representation was abandoned.

The real-method probe uses source files bundled from each pinned worktree, avoiding dependence on pre-existing `dist/` freshness. The head fixture sets chunk/inline/result/aggregate to 4/8/12/24 bytes. Capture produces 4 + 4 + 2 byte records; base produces one 10-byte record. Both decode to the same text. A five-byte codec or worker message passes the base limit and is rejected under the head fixture's four-byte ceiling. These observations teach policy propagation; they are not an end-to-end parity result.

## What I would drop

The oversized opening title and tiny secondary module labels. The open readings are lengthy, but the representation cannot honestly encode error provenance or adapter precedence without words. The inner inspector scrollbar also costs discoverability; the full source book and open readings provide a simpler reading path.

## What I would do next

Ask a fresh reader to distinguish the chunk strand from the three 250 ms strands, then compare two consumers while holding Receipts fixed. Compare their explanation with one produced from an ordinary dependency diagram. No human comprehension trial was run.

## Time spent

Approximately one hour, including required reading, source inspection, library evaluation, implementation, method recording, browser checks and documentation.

## Visual-variable legend

| Variable | Encoded fact | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Row | Curated consumer family | Multiple named classes can be grouped; these are not processes or reference counts. |
| Column | Actual `DaemonPolicyValues` slice | Seven slices remain fixed at every reading depth. |
| Vertical strand | One exact policy leaf | Crossing an unrelated row without a knot does not connect that row. Strand length is not measured reach or runtime traffic. |
| Color | Capacity ochre; time teal; memory violet; recovery rust | Purpose categories are an authored reading aid, not types in the repository. Values carry units in the inspector. |
| Circle / diamond knot | Leaf appears in several drawn families / only one drawn family | A diamond does not imply only one method or call site in the repository. |
| Heavy / light tie | Family reads a required value / forwards a slice to another shown family | Required refers to the input contract; it does not mean every constructor validates policy at runtime. |
| Solid / dashed cell rim, `U` | Stated adoption reason / specific rationale gap on the open surface | A dashed rim does not mean unvalidated, incorrect or more severe. General reasons can coexist with specific gaps. |
| Highlight | Selected exact leaf, equal-value set, or two delivery fields | Highlight changes inspection only. It does not edit policy or simulate execution. |
| Depth control | Surface, wiring or exact receipts at the same coordinate | No semantic zoom; matrix position and geometry do not change. |
| Recorded bar width | Bytes per output record in the saved probe | Injected tiny policy fixture; no daemon, socket or performance measurement. |

The source map intentionally omits `resources.effectiveMemoryBytes` as a direct consumer leaf: it belongs to central derivation. The map also omits transitive references and composition sites outside the named family inventory. Its 38 leaves are an authored route model, not a compiler census. See [field-map.md](evidence/field-map.md).

## Libraries considered and used

| Option | Evaluation |
| --- | --- |
| [D3 band scales](https://d3js.org/d3-scale/band), [data joins](https://d3js.org/d3-selection/joining), symbol shapes | **Used.** Nested band scales place slices, families and leaves. D3 joins render stable crossings and thread selection. SVG makes one strand continuous across cell boundaries. No custom graph layout, diagram router or camera engine was needed. |
| [AG Grid cell components](https://www.ag-grid.com/javascript-data-grid/component-cell-renderer/) | Considered. Its grid interactions are attractive, but a continuous leaf crossing several rendered cells would still need a separate overlay. Spreadsheet editing, sorting and virtualization do not help this fixed 7 × 7 comparison. |
| [Handsontable cell renderers](https://handsontable.com/docs/javascript-data-grid/cell-renderer/) | Considered. Appropriate for cell-oriented data manipulation; this read-only artifact needs continuous strands and a depth coordinate outside the grid. |
| [Observable Plot cell mark](https://observablehq.github.io/plot/marks/cell) | Considered. A strong compact matrix alternative. Multiple leaf knots, mixed forwarding weights and independent coordinate focus fit direct D3 selection more naturally here. |
| CSS Grid | Used for page/inspector layout. D3 supplies the matrix's mature rendering and coordinate helpers. |

Runtime dependencies are bundled locally with [third-party notices](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt). No hosted fonts, APIs or network requests are required to read the artifact.

## What the form teaches better or worse

The same vertical line can enforce different jobs without splitting into unrelated arrows: capture, spool, codec and worker all use the chunk leaf. Conversely, three aligned-looking 250 ms values remain physically separate strands in different slices. Circle/diamond shape and heavy/light ties let a reader separate sharing from forwarding. Keeping depth fixed makes comparison a change of address rather than a fresh descent through a hierarchy.

A conventional diagram would label each relationship more directly and scale better when only a few relationships matter. The loom's geometry uses space for empty crossings and its smallest labels need the inspector. It does not explain recovery error provenance, test deletion or normalization through cloth alone; those receive open readings and paired receipts. These are design judgments, not measured learning outcomes.

## Evidence and verification

- [Source model](evidence/model.json): 44 pinned full sources, 72 exact receipts, fields, cells, open readings and the complete 60-file diff inventory. [Supplied patch](evidence/diff.patch) is preserved.
- [Pyramid map](evidence/pyramid-map.md): every open decision/surprise and its deeper entry and receipts. Full-file context is raw audit material and can contain unrelated implementation detail.
- [Capture checks](evidence/capture-checks.json) and [static checks](evidence/static-checks.json): source/Git/hash equality, unchanged central policy and policy tests, the unused base startup timeout, all displayed field values, local links and clean tracked worktrees.
- [Probe](evidence/probe.json): actual base/head capture and two validator methods, with expected records/results asserted before saving. No Symnav test suite or full daemon was executed; test excerpts describe source only.
- [Browser checks](evidence/browser-checks.json): 147 coordinate/depth visits; commuting keyboard movement; all fifteen active crossings; all 38 exact thread selections; three comparison modes; reading/source returns; history; source-dialog focus; 320/390/768/1024/1440 px layouts; SVG text bounds; print; offline file opening; JavaScript-disabled readings/source book; and touch controls. Final checks report no page errors, external runtime requests or failed HTTP requests. The [targeted final check](evidence/final-browser-checks.json) covers the added base-constructor receipt, corrected source-book counts and final recovery wording. Together the passes exercise all 72 modal receipts. A stale open browser document caused one retained check timeout; reloading the rebuilt bundle resolved it.
- [Screenshots](screenshots/): desktop opening, full fabric, equal values, shared chunk probe, recovery receipt and phone depth. Desktop, source and phone views were visually inspected.

No Symnav source or branch was modified, committed, rebased or pushed. The experiment's existing brief and harness log were preserved. Shared campaign index, queue and commits are left to the orchestrator.

## Regeneration

With the supplied worktrees still at their pins, run from this folder:

```sh
npm ci
npm run capture
npm run probe
npm run build
npm run verify
```

For browser checks, run `npm run serve`, then `npm run check` in another terminal. Checks use installed Google Chrome. `LOOM_URL` can select a different local server URL. These tools write only inside this experiment. Reading the generated page requires none of them.

# daemon-weather-map

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html) directly:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/73-daemon-weather-map/index.html
```

No installation, server, network connection, or worktree is needed to read the built page. **Main / #149** changes the ownership weather. **Failure pressure** selects four illustrative conditions. Select an **H**, the package front, or forecast haze to inspect its decision. **Trace this weather** follows the selected failure condition. **Previous / Next** traverses all six readings; Escape closes source, then the reading, and restores focus. Reading fragments and browser Back work. **+ / − / Fit**, dragging, and pinching magnify the chart. Motion can be paused and respects reduced-motion preferences.

Desktop is the best surface for comparing the complete field. On a phone the fitted map is an overview; magnify and pan to read its labels. The complete bulletin, unrolled mechanisms, and standalone source receipts also work without JavaScript.

## Kind

page, animated

## Subjects

`stack`: main `b6801ebdd2421d0ca2e4bdd61ec0f04c24ddd73e` → #149 `d07002357d3e9596bfaae910a1ac63b77981620b`.

The narrow teaching subject is **the client’s two recovery scopes and their ownership move**. A result fetch retains transfer state; an identical-request reattachment allocates fresh delivery state. This is not a complete inventory of all 26 PRs. PRs #138, #139, #142, #147, #148 and #149 provide the main explanations; #131 supplies additional policy context within the assigned stack.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: learner reading a synoptic weather chart. Assigned angle: architecture as changing weather, with exact named mappings and explicit limits.
- Box lenses: static source/package ownership and runtime request/result flow. Four selected client roles cross the package front while their process boundary stays fixed. Shared files may have other callers; the process placement depicts this selected path.
- Opening style: picture and a marked weather analogy, under “The connection breaks. The request stays.”
- Shape: complete chart, legend, and six open bulletin readings → selected mechanism → pinned source. The headline alone is not the complete layer.
- Navigation: weather stations and conditions provide nonlinear entry; the six numbered readings, Previous/Next, and unrolled source book provide a linear route. Dialogs preserve the reader’s place.
- Trust posture: distinguish source observations, stated preservation reasons, an unexplained exact calibration, illustrative scenarios, and executed tests. No correctness verdict or review collection.
- Persona: a TypeScript-familiar teammate who knows Symnav but not its daemon recovery path.
- Representations used: two contour fields, selected-role pressure counts, a moving package front, a fixed process divider, animated request/result vectors, condition-dependent precipitation, forecast hatching, retained/fresh/disposed state labels, a complete bulletin, and local source receipts.
- Importance rule: distinguish a delivery attempt from accepted execution first; then ownership, durable receipt, recovery exhaustion, policy scope and rationale, and test evidence. No risk score.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): read-only main/tip source, policy record, architecture specification, Git blobs/status, and focused existing test execution. Bundle used: `inputs/stack/pr.json` including PR bodies and commit messages; a direct before/tip diff of the scoped transport test file was generated. No implementing conversation or production trace was supplied. Precomputed overviews were not used.
- Tech: D3 7.9.0; esbuild 0.25.10 for a local classic-script bundle; Python source capture and verification; Playwright 1.61.1 with system Google Chrome. Native HTML dialogs, system fonts, and SVG. Codex; no subagents.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): **04-textbook-chapter**, **23-zoom-canvas**, **36-be-weird-a**, **37-be-weird-b**, and **53-be-weird-53** informed evidence honesty, complete-layer coverage, and return navigation. **67-blast-radius-terrain** was read to avoid repeating its elevated policy-reader terrain: this chart instead compares source concentration and recovery conditions on a flat moving field. **61-pixel-causality-grid**, **63-daemon-constellation**, and other finished README representation fields informed the novelty survey. No predecessor implementation, measurements, decision register, or source bank was copied. The [survey](evidence/novelty-survey.json) covers 70 finished READMEs and found no weather/forecast representation.

## What I tried

I considered a broader transport concentration count, including framing. That would blur existing standalone codecs and make the “pressure” denominator hard to defend. The final census names only four roles: socket I/O, accepted recovery, transfer continuity, and output capture. Three share one source file on main; the fourth has a separate CLI file. Each has a separate package file at the tip.

I evaluated D3, deck.gl and MapLibre before choosing a planar SVG chart. No full representation was abandoned. The first screenshots exposed a before-state label collision and tiny fitted phone labels. I moved the collision and added D3 optical zoom. Receiver/capture labels now change with the condition, so persistence is visible on the field. The exhausted-fetch result wind stops at its terminal marker.

The initial browser check raced the asynchronous media-preference event. A second run exposed that zero-duration D3 transitions still deferred the front update. The check now waits for the actual preference, and reduced-motion snapshot changes assign the final geometry immediately. Draft screenshots and failed check records remain under [evidence/attempts](evidence/attempts/).

## What I would drop

The outermost contour bands add atmosphere but carry less than the H count and named owner. The full source files are useful for auditing but bulky for normal reading. Optical zoom rescues phone labels while losing the simultaneous overview.

## What I would do next

Ask an unfamiliar reader to predict what survives a fetch versus a reattachment, then ask whether the moving front implies a process move. Compare those explanations with ones elicited by a conventional sequence diagram. No human comprehension trial was run here.

## Time spent

Approximately 45 minutes of active work, including reading, source reconciliation, construction, focused test runs, and browser inspection.

## Visual-variable legend

| Variable | Encoded fact | Explicit limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H numeral | Number of the **four selected roles** owned in one source file: main `3 + 1`; tip `1 + 1 + 1 + 1` | Counts are a bounded, authored role census, not all responsibilities, classes, lines of code, runtime load, complexity, or risk. |
| Green contour nesting | Illustrative concentration around each source-file owner; higher H gets more nested contours | Interpolated field, ring radii and positions are synthetic. No physical pressure units or geographic meaning. |
| Rust line and triangles | Source package front: the selected implementations move from `apps/cli` to `packages/daemon` | Its travel interpolates the two endpoints. It does not reconstruct intermediate commits. #148 staging and #149 switching are named in reading 01. |
| Fixed dashed vertical line | Client process / daemon process separation on the selected warm path | Omits the worker, server internals, and other callers of shared modules. Package ownership does not determine process residence. |
| Blue rightward vectors | Execute or result-fetch request, named on the wind | Local calls are simplified. The socket hop is at the process divider; speeds and dash spacing do not measure latency or traffic. |
| Amber leftward vectors | Result records; the terminal marker cuts off exhausted fetch delivery | Motion is illustrative, not a captured execution. No result is depicted as returned after the terminal marker. |
| Station status text | Receiver/capture retained on fetch; fresh on reattachment; disposed on terminal failure | Record 0 and offset 1 are an authored example, not a recorded production incident. “Durable” follows the code’s awaited append contract; it does not assert crash-proof filesystem persistence. |
| Rust rain texture | The reader’s selected failure condition | Rain area, density, speed, and opacity encode neither probability nor severity. “Clear” is a selected completed-delivery example, not a health verdict. |
| Hatched forecast oval, U | No specific calibration found for exactly **one** reattachment and **one** fetch per attempt | Uncertainty concerns rationale. The code values and distinct counter scopes are known. General preservation and purpose are stated. |

## Libraries considered and used

| Option | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| [D3 contours](https://d3js.org/d3-contour/contour) and geoPath/geoIdentity | Used to extract and render planar contour polygons from the illustrative scalar fields. No custom contouring algorithm. |
| [D3 transitions](https://d3js.org/d3-transition), shape curves and zoom | Used for front interpolation, contour crossfade, vector motion, smooth geometry, optical zoom, pan and pinch. There is no hand-written animation clock, graph layout, routing engine, or semantic zoom. Coordinates are an explicitly authored conceptual geography. |
| [deck.gl layers](https://deck.gl/docs/api-reference/core/layer) | Considered for GPU rendering and picking. Four owners and accessible source entry points fit SVG without a GPU layer stack. |
| [MapLibre custom layers](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/interfaces/CustomLayerInterface/) | Considered for map interaction and custom weather overlays. This subject has no geographic coordinates or basemap; D3’s planar field and zoom suit the data more directly. |

The built page makes no external requests. Library licenses are included in [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt).

## What the weird form teaches better or worse

The intended advantage is seeing **three independent things at once**: responsibility concentration changes, source ownership crosses a front, and the process boundary remains fixed. Changing the failure condition leaves the same ownership field in place while receiver/capture state changes. That distinguishes “a connection ended” from “the accepted request needs to execute again.”

A conventional sequence diagram would show the precise conditional order and two nested counters more directly. The weather field gives arbitrary spatial geometry too much apparent authority unless the legend stays nearby. It also cannot carry the exact authenticated-close predicate or explain why a numeric default was chosen; those need the bulletin and source. These are design judgments, not measured comprehension gains.

- [Rationale search](evidence/rationale-search.json): relevant matches in supplied stack PR bodies and commit messages. The policy record supplies purposes and defaults; no specific numerical calibration was found in the inspected record.
- [Main run](main-tests.log): **34 tests passed**, one existing transport suite. [Tip run](head-tests.log): **80 tests passed**, transport, receiver, and execution-client suites. The transport tests use controlled real Unix sockets; these logs are not a production daemon trace or whole-stack parity result.
- [Test census](evidence/test-census.json): all fourteen literal `it(...)` titles from the selected main transport file remain at the tip; parameterized cases are excluded from this title count. [Full scoped diff](evidence/transport-test.diff) preserves migration and assertion changes. Matching titles do not establish unchanged assertions.
- [Browser checks](evidence/browser-checks.json): twelve passing groups covering direct file opening, both snapshots, all four conditions, all six readings and 42 receipts, source expansion, keyboard/focus returns, history, zoom, touch, motion/reduced motion, 320/390/768/1440 layouts, and JavaScript-disabled source access. No page errors, console errors, external runtime requests, or horizontal page overflow were found in the final run.
- [Static checks](evidence/static-checks.json): source hashes/Git correspondence, selected-role counts, receipt bounds and key predicates, links and anchors, displayed test counts, and clean tracked worktree status.
- [Screenshots](screenshots/): final main/tip, exhausted-fetch, source and phone captures were visually inspected. Drafts and negative check results remain in the attempts folder.

Only this experiment folder was authored. Symnav source and branches were not modified, committed, pushed, or rebased. Index and campaign queue handling are left to the orchestrator. The artifact has no verdict buttons, comment storage, or response collection.

## Regeneration

Opening the built page requires none of these commands. With the supplied worktrees present at the recorded pins, run from this folder:

```sh

npm run capture

```

Browser checks use system Google Chrome; `WEATHER_CHROME` can select another executable. The capture/build scripts do not rerun Symnav tests. Logs in this folder preserve the completed runs.

README
# admission-circuit-board

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html) directly:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/72-admission-circuit-board/index.html
```

No installation, server, network, or worktree is needed to use the built artifact. JavaScript is required. The opening shows a completed two-scope recovery. **Trace again** follows its signal; **Step**, the stage slider, and **Show outcome** support inspection at any pace. Choose a preset or change the switches. Click a component or one of the eight readings for mechanism and frozen source. Escape returns focus to the opener.

Drag to pan; use **Fit board** or **Follow signal** to change scale. On a phone, the fitted circuit is an overview; Follow signal enlarges the current component. The complete readings remain normal-sized text.

## Kind

other: interactive simulation — an offline circuit board with source-executed admission/retry gates and modeled I/O.

## Subjects

`stack`: main `b6801ebdd2421d0ca2e4bdd61ec0f04c24ddd73e` → #149 `d07002357d3e9596bfaae910a1ac63b77981620b`.

Narrow teaching scope: **what permits a warm request to fall back locally, and what recovery remains after acceptance**. Relevant slices are #133–134 (failure/admission authority), #137–139 (transport/transfer ownership), #142 (execution recovery), and #148–149 (staging and active package ownership). This is not a decision inventory for all 26 PRs. Cache lifetimes, worker replacement, startup election, policy beyond these recovery counters, and the full stack's test changes are outside the explanation.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: learner operating a fault-injection instrument; no verdicts or response collection.
- Box lenses: source package ownership and caller/daemon/host process boundaries, kept distinct through the board enclosure and package stamps.
- Opening style: completed recovery circuit and the marked acceptance-latch analogy; before/after ownership strip.
- Shape: complete stopping layer = opening, circuit, legend, simulation caveat and eight open readings. Matching mechanism/source dialogs deepen those readings. The headline alone is not the complete layer.
- Navigation: linear signal stepping and numbered readings; nonlinear switches, component inspection, source selection and geometric pan/zoom. Dialogs have previous/next and focus-preserving return. No semantic zoom.
- Trust posture: source-derived simulation, conservative stated/unexplained reasons, frozen source receipts, controlled actual-client probes, and bounded test results. No correctness verdict or whole-stack parity assertion.
- Persona: a TypeScript teammate who understands a request/response exchange but has not learned this daemon's acceptance boundary.
- Representations used: ordered gate chain; route multiplexer; consistency fuse; local-permit OR gate; acceptance latch; two recovery counters; colored orthogonal traces; outcome LEDs; package/process stamps; controlled failure presets; exact source excerpts.
- Importance rule: authority to start local execution first, then delivery state, first-failure vocabulary, recovery scope, physical ownership and evidence limits.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): pinned main/head source and test files; contributor guidance and architecture/policy specifications; Git object/hash verification; built head modules; 13 controlled execution-client probes and a real ledger deduplication probe; five focused source test files; Chromium interaction and screenshot checks. Bundle inputs used: selected PR bodies and commit records from `pr.json`, `stack.md`, and selected `diff.patch` sections. Precomputed overviews were not used.
- Tech: React 19.3.0, React Flow 12.11.6, ELK.js 0.11.1, GSAP 3.15.0 with MotionPathPlugin, esbuild 0.25.12; Python capture; Node recording/checking; Playwright 1.63.0 with system Chrome. All browser assets are bundled locally; system fonts; no generated bitmap assets.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): no reused implementation, evidence, or content. Read 04-textbook-chapter, 23-zoom-canvas, 36-be-weird-a, 37-be-weird-b, and 53-be-weird-53 in full for their evidence and interaction standard. Surveyed available 01–68 README representation/opening fields, with particular attention to 15-message-choreography-sim, 22-game-any, 25-reader-sketch, 61-pixel-causality-grid, 62-policy-stained-glass, 63-daemon-constellation, 65-decision-tetris, 66-boundary-subway and 68-semantic-zoom-microscope. No subagents were used.

## What I tried

Considered putting every routing and admission guard on one long graph. Experiment 68 already concentrates on routing precedence, and that design would obscure the acceptance boundary. The final board compresses routing into a supplied snapshot and spends its space on admission authority and the two recovery circuits.

Compared Rete's execution engine with React Flow plus ELK. The graph is read-only and the admission/retry classes can execute unchanged; a second graph execution engine was unnecessary. ELK computes all component positions, ports and orthogonal trace routes. The tiny ordered gate glyphs inside U2 are a static source-order illustration.

The first browser image exposed a black library background and undersized gate text. I replaced the background, tightened ELK spacing and enlarged the lettering. The opening now shows a completed recovery trace. Tests caught non-editable nodes swallowing pointer events and dialog removal losing focus; both were fixed. The simulation audit also corrected admission-sample counts for a reattachment: it makes another authenticated execute attempt, even though the drawn loop abbreviates repeated admission.

Early images and two failed browser-check reports are retained in [attempts](attempts). No complete representation was abandoned.

## What I would drop

The component subtitles are secondary at overview scale. The process stamps also require the legend; a conventional swimlane has a lower decoding cost. The phone overview is a locator, not a comfortable way to read every gate simultaneously.

## What I would do next

Ask a fresh reader to predict the two simultaneous-failure case and the contradictory retry-bit case, then compare with the same facts in a conventional flowchart. No human comprehension study was performed here.

## Time spent

About 35 minutes, including source inspection, library evaluation, probes, construction, browser fixes and documentation.

## Visual-variable legend

| Channel | What it encodes |
| --- | --- |
| Gate shape | Multiplexer = first route; ordered AND-like gates = admission priority; fuse = rejection consistency; OR = local retry authority; D/Q latch = retained acceptance. These are explicitly mnemonic, not literal digital logic. |
| Trace color | Amber = admission rejection vocabulary; rose = transport failures/uncertainty; violet = accepted execution failures; cyan = delivery recovery; pale green = signal/result or local permit. Wires also have directional arrowheads. |
| Component package | Single outline / C = caller-process daemon mechanism; double outline / D = daemon-process admission; H = host-supplied local execution. The green enclosure identifies final daemon package ownership, with H explicitly external. |
| LED state | Bright outcome LED = selected outcome; dark = not reached. Admission LEDs distinguish passed and failed gates. The acceptance latch remains lit after a terminal failure. |
| Hatching | `//` marks a later guard that the signal never reached. Two faults can therefore expose a visible priority decision. |
| Counter enclosure | One reattachment allowance belongs to the request; one fetch allowance belongs to each execute attempt. Counts are modeled events, not performance measurements. |
| Motion | One bright pulse follows the selected trace. Motion and geometric distance carry order, never duration or electrical behavior. Reduced motion removes the pulse while preserving stepping. |

## Libraries considered and used

| Library | Evaluation |
| --- | --- |
| [Rete.js engine](https://retejs.org/docs/concepts/engine/) | Considered its dataflow/control-flow engines. Useful for editable executable graphs, but this instrument needs fixed topology and direct source policy execution. Not used. |
| [React Flow](https://reactflow.dev/learn/layouting/layouting) | Used for custom nodes/edges, viewport navigation, zoom controls and keyboard-accessible component controls. Its layout overview helped separate rendering from layout. |
| [ELK Layered](https://eclipse.dev/elk/reference/algorithms/org-eclipse-elk-layered.html) | Used for all graph placement and orthogonal routing with constrained ports, including the backward recovery edge. A good match for circuit-style wiring. Dagre was considered through the React Flow comparison; the port and routing controls favored ELK. |
| [GSAP MotionPathPlugin](https://gsap.com/docs/v3/Plugins/MotionPathPlugin/) | Used to animate the signal on the actual ELK path. GSAP also schedules playback; no custom animation or pan/zoom engine. |

Versions are recorded in `package-lock.json`. The generated `app.js.LEGAL.txt` retains bundled library notices.

## What the circuit form teaches

The strongest feature is the **absence of an energized local path** after acceptance. Recovery lights another circuit while the local LED remains dark. The fuse makes a wire Boolean visibly subordinate to code authority. The ordered gate chain makes a later conflicting duplicate remain unobserved when draining already failed. These are changes a reader can cause and compare, not decoration around a card summary.

A conventional flowchart would need less explanation of symbols and would show process placement more directly. This board compresses calls into traces and abbreviates reattachment; it cannot establish concurrency, latency, resource consumption, or an actual host execution count. The claimed teaching benefits are design judgments, not measured learning gains.

## Evidence and verification

- [Source manifest](evidence/source-manifest.json): 31 frozen documents. Every captured worktree source equals its pinned Git object. The UI contains 49 selected excerpts, including explicit rationale receipts.
- [Controlled probes](evidence/probes.json): 13 runs of the actual compiled head execution client with scripted sockets, fake empty-output capture and ACK stub. Includes pre-write refusal, uncertain close, normal/contradictory rejections, accepted terminal failure, both recovery paths and both exhaustion paths. The ledger probe reuses the same actual entry for a matching request. These are not live-daemon traces.
- [Focused source tests](evidence/focused-tests.log): 147 tests passed across five files: admission, client routing/fallback, protocol validation, direct execution client and socket execution delivery. This includes existing real socket and mixed-stream transfer tests. The daemon package build passed. The whole repository suite was not run.
- [Artifact checks](evidence/artifact-checks.json): the model agrees with all 13 recorded client cases on outcomes and I/O counts; 576 admission combinations preserve the acceptance/no-local-replay invariant; source hashes, all excerpt bounds and ELK component bounds pass.
- [Browser checks](evidence/browser-checks.json): preset/field interactions, all board components, all source receipts, source previous/next and Escape focus return, playback/pause/step, keyboard slider, pan/zoom/fit/follow, 1440/768/390/320 layouts, reduced motion and direct `file://` opening. No external runtime requests or browser errors in the passing run.
- [Screenshots](screenshots): final overview, precedence and corruption states, source detail, and a phone view were visually inspected.
- [Pyramid map](evidence/pyramid-map.md): authored details and visible top-layer parents. The two rationale gaps are the original priority's justification and the quantitative basis for exactly-one recovery defaults; the preservation rationale itself is stated.

Both symnav worktrees remained clean for tracked files. All source edits and generated artifacts are in this experiment; allowed build/test outputs stayed in the worktree's build/cache locations. No commits, pushes, branch changes, comment storage, verdicts or review persistence.

## Rebuild and repeat

Opening the artifact needs none of these commands. From this folder:

```sh
npm ci
python3 scripts/capture.py
npm run build
npm test
```

With the supplied head worktree pinned and built, `node scripts/probe.mjs` regenerates the controlled receipts. It does not run a daemon or mutate the source. The original focused source test command was:

```sh
cd ~/projects/rich-review-v2/worktrees/stack-head/packages/daemon
pnpm exec vitest run src/daemon-admission.test.ts src/client/daemon-client.test.ts src/transport/protocol-validator.test.ts src/transport/execution-client.test.ts src/transport/daemon-transport-execution.test.ts
```

For the browser suite, run `npm start` from the experiment (localhost:8472), then `node scripts/browser-check.mjs` in another terminal. System Chrome is required for that check script. [brief.md](brief.md) preserves the received assignment.
