# pixel-causality-grid

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html) directly:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/61-pixel-causality-grid/index.html
```

No install, server, network or worktree is needed to read the artifact. D3 and the evidence are local. JavaScript draws the interactive field; the complete boundary key, package/test decisions and linked source inventory also work without it.

Select a pixel to inspect its revision and owner. Arrow keys move between boundaries and PR heads; Home/End reach main/#149; Enter opens the inspector; **Return to selected pixel** restores focus. Boundary letters jump directly into evidence. Browser Back and fragments retain the selected coordinate. Playback supports stepping, scrubbing, pause, two source builds and three controlled outcomes. Nothing is collected or saved from the reader.

## Kind

page, interactive

## Subjects

stack — all 26 supplied PR heads, plus main as a baseline. Main `b6801ebdd2421d0ca2e4bdd61ec0f04c24ddd73e` → #149 `d07002357d3e9596bfaae910a1ac63b77981620b`.

The narrow subject is **the lifetime of an accepted turn across terminal publication, delivery, FIFO sampling and acknowledgement**. The field has 243 concrete boundary instances: nine boundaries at 27 revisions. It does not claim 243 unique decisions or an explanation of every other change in the stack.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: learner reading a causal instrument; assigned angle is the pixel causality field.
- Box lenses: static module/package ownership, plus runtime object/lifecycle authority. CLI process, daemon process and worker thread remain distinct from package ownership.
- Opening style: a short completion paradox and a simultaneous ownership field. The visibly separate ACK branch supplies the early intuition; schematic distances are marked.
- Shape: complete field/key and two visible package/test decisions → controlled recording and selected mechanism → exact pinned source. The complete stopping layer spans more than one viewport and has an explicit end marker.
- Navigation: a fixed coordinate grid, linear boundary controls, a six-checkpoint replay, direct links, browser history and return focus. There is no semantic zoom.
- Trust posture: distinguish implemented order from author rationale. Seven boundary families have a specific stated reason; two exact ordering rationales were not found. Package staging has a stated reason; the precise readiness-timing assertion deletions are unexplained. No correctness verdict.
- Persona: a teammate who knows symnav but has not followed the daemon refactor.
- Representations used: a 27 × 9 ownership raster, compound symbols, an ACK branch, physical-package cutover enclosure, two moving request indicators tied to recorded checkpoints, process/thread containment, exact source excerpts, a textual source inventory and a test diff.
- Importance rule: expose what prevents the next turn, which owner controls that barrier, and what is independent of it. Preserve rationale gaps, staging and changed test observation at the top.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): read-only Git objects for all 26 heads and main; source for the process shell, accepted-execution session, generation manager, ledger, queue, delivery, lifetime and CLI composition; architecture/follow-up specs; the #148 readiness test rename/diff; new controlled source-method recordings. Bundle use: all 26 PR context/decision sections, commit-message rationale search, revision pins and relevant `repo-rules.md`. Symbol overview placeholders were not used as evidence. The supplied net diff was not needed; the scoped historical diff was generated directly from pinned objects.
- Tech: D3 7.9.0, SVG, native HTML/CSS/JavaScript; Python capture/build/verification; Node with the prepared worktree's `tsx` loader for source recording; isolated Playwright with system Chrome for checks. No generated images, remote fonts or hosted services. Harness: Codex; no delegated agents.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): read the required 04-textbook-chapter, 23-zoom-canvas, 36-be-weird-a, 37-be-weird-b and 53-be-weird-53 READMEs in order; surveyed representation/shape declarations across 01–60; read 51-angle-new-subject-51's README and 23's decision inventory. Borrowed the standards for bounded recordings, exact receipts, explicit unknown reasons and return navigation. No predecessor implementation, dataset, probe or screenshot was copied. The #148 test claim was independently checked against its original Git diff.

## What I tried

Initially considered a PR-column field of the 117 authored decisions. It would mainly encode a large prose inventory and make the narrow runtime dependency harder to see. Before implementing it, changed the axes to **revision × the same nine boundary events**. This makes both retained structure and eventual extraction visible at once.

The first raster was too tall: the ownership split fell below the initial desktop viewport. Smaller pixels and tighter row bands brought #145–#149 into view without hiding early PRs. The first playback had overlapping headers and a clipped ACK caption; separate letters and shorter labels fixed both. A 768 px browser check found the source pane's intrinsic width expanding the page; allowing the grid item to shrink fixed it. The initial failure report is preserved in [browser-checks-initial.json](evidence/browser-checks-initial.json).

The probe used actual source coordination on main and tip, with independently held worker, delivery, sampling and cleanup ports. Both builds exhibit the chosen distinction: a completed ledger entry can still hold the FIFO; delivery settling is followed by a sampling gate; ordinary ACK remains independent. A sampling rejection releases its boundary after diagnosis. A valid ACK still succeeds when injected cleanup rejects. This is a controlled observation, not a production daemon trace or a parity claim about all PRs.

No completed representation was abandoned. Rejected design options and UI corrections are retained here rather than presented as negative findings about symnav.

## What I would drop

The source inventory table duplicates the per-pixel receipts, but earns a place as the JavaScript-free and keyboard-independent route. The first 22 rows, including main, contain little ownership variation in this lens; their repetition is evidence, but a reader already familiar with that fact may prefer a collapsed band. On a phone, the field requires horizontal scrolling and loses much of its simultaneous comparison benefit.

## What I would do next

Give a maintainer only the complete stopping layer, then ask when B can start and whether cleanup rejection withholds ACK. Compare their explanation with a conventional sequence diagram using the same facts; no human comprehension study was performed here.

## Time spent

Approximately 30 minutes, including required reading, source capture, new recordings, implementation, browser inspection and documentation.

## Visual-variable legend

| Variable | Factual meaning | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vertical position | main, then the 26 supplied PR heads in stack/dependency order | Equal spacing is not elapsed development time. |
| Horizontal position | A–G: the selected successful-turn dependencies. H–I: the separate result-ACK branch | Equal spacing is not latency. ACK is not a required step after G. Workspace-deletion shutdown is the explicitly named exception to ordinary ACK independence. |
| Hue | The module owning the selected operation/state: process shell (ochre), execution session (mint), generation manager (coral), ledger (violet), delivery session (blue), queue (lime) | This is local ownership, not authorship or file size. A stable hue does not establish unchanged code. |
| Shape | Square: publish/retain state; diamond: await gate; triangle: dispatch; circle: side effect | A categorical mechanism key, not a UML vocabulary. |
| Saturation | Saturated: a specific stated reason in the inspected stack prose; desaturated: no specific rationale found | S does not mean the reason was first stated at that row's date. U is scoped to inspected material, not a claim about all possible conversations. Neither grades correctness. Textual S/U labels repeat the distinction. |
| Row enclosure | #149 is the active physical `@symnav/daemon` boundary | #148 stages package code while the active CLI path remains in `apps/cli`. |
| White moving outline | The boundary reached by the recorded A checkpoint; B has a dashed outline | Playback interpolation and spacing are illustrative. Recorded states are authoritative; motion is not a measured trace duration. No autoplay on opening. |
| Selection outline | The exact cell whose source is being read | Separate from the white playback position; selection does not modify symnav. |

The ownership unit is explicit per column: A is acceptance coordination; B is worker-generation readiness/execution; C is the caller's seal await; D is ledger publication; E is the tracked delivery promise owner; F is sampling scheduling; G is the FIFO scheduler; H/I are ACK coordination. For E, the blue delivery owner supplies the promise while the execution coordinator awaits it. Each E receipt includes both sides.

## Libraries considered and used

**Used D3 7.9.0** for categorical band/point placement, keyed SVG data joins, mechanism symbols, colors, easing, transitions and playback timing. At 243 cells, retaining an individual accessible element per pixel was useful. No graph layout, routing engine, semantic camera or animation loop was hand-written. Native overflow handles small screens; this is an ordered grid rather than an arbitrary graph.

Considered [PixiJS scene objects](https://pixijs.com/8.x/guides/components/scene-objects) for a larger GPU field, but this scale benefits more from direct SVG focus/source association. Considered [Observable Plot's cell mark](https://observablehq.github.io/plot/marks/cell); the design would also need symbol layers and custom per-cell navigation, so direct D3 was a better fit for this artifact. Regl was considered only at the sketch stage, with no prototype. These choices were design evaluations, not renderer benchmarks.

Consulted the official [D3 band-scale documentation](https://d3js.org/d3-scale/band) and [transition documentation](https://d3js.org/d3-transition). The pinned distribution and [license](vendor/d3.LICENSE) are vendored. The artifact makes no external requests.

## What the weird form taught better or worse

**Better:** simultaneous repetition makes the distinction between a retained causal order and an ownership extraction visible. Three small color changes near the bottom replace an entire process-shell column family; #148's staged copy does not masquerade as a production cutover. The ledger's terminal column and the delivery/sample columns remain spatially separate, and the moving outline can stop after “completed” while B remains at acceptance. ACK occupies its own branch rather than appearing as the next box in a misleading total order.

**Worse:** the field cannot explain a missing author rationale through color alone, or represent a duplicate-attachment promise map with full fidelity. Exact reasons and the latest-promise qualification still require short text. A conventional sequence diagram is quicker for one revision and can show the call/return edges more explicitly. The grid earns its space only when comparing the stack's owners; its quiet early region is expensive on small screens.

## Evidence, scope and verification

- [Field data](evidence/field.json) and [capture manifest](evidence/capture.json): all 243 coordinates, revision pins and 105 frozen source/prose documents. Each cell's excerpt is checked against its own Git revision. Full receipts include SHA-256 and line anchors.
- [Recordings](evidence/recordings.json): main and tip × normal, sampling rejection, cleanup rejection; six runs and 36 checkpoints. Real main `WorkspaceDaemon` methods use a prototype instance with controlled dependencies. Tip uses real `AcceptedExecutionSession` and `DaemonDeliverySession`; both use their real queue and ledger. Worker, spool, filesystem, clock and send behavior are fake ports. Two new request IDs plus one identical duplicate yield two actual worker starts and two navigation-acceptance resets. No sockets, process startup, disk durability, production latency, generation transitions or full-stack parity were measured.
- [Static verification](evidence/verification.json): cell coverage, source hashes, excerpt bounds, seal/publication/delivery ordering at all 27 snapshots, recorded gates, local destinations and clean tracked status of both worktrees.
- [Browser checks](evidence/browser-checks.json): every cell, keyboard/return navigation, history and fragments, source dialogs, all recordings, playback controls, SVG label bounds, responsive widths, reduced motion, print, JavaScript-disabled reading and direct offline file opening. [Screenshots](screenshots/) were visually inspected; the initial responsive failure and its screenshot are retained.
- [Readiness test patch](evidence/readiness-test.patch): exact #147 → #148 rename-aware diff. The page exposes the changed fixture and removed duration expectations, without claiming repository-wide absence of timing tests. Existing symnav test suites were not run for this experiment; the new source-method probes were executed.

Rationale search covered the supplied PR contexts/decisions and commit messages, relevant repository rules, and the architecture/follow-up specs. An original pre-stack design rationale or implementing conversation may exist outside those inputs. General preservation intent was not used to invent a specific reason for C or D.

No symnav source, branch or worktree was modified. The artifact has no verdict, approval, comment, score or review-storage controls. Queue, index and campaign completion handling are left to the orchestrator.

## Regeneration

Opening the page needs none of these commands. With the supplied worktrees available, from this folder:

```sh
python3 scripts/capture.py
python3 scripts/build.py
python3 scripts/verify.py
```

To regenerate the recordings from source, from the repository root:

```sh
node --import ./worktrees/stack-head/apps/cli/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs experiments/61-pixel-causality-grid/scripts/record.mjs
```

For optional browser verification, serve this folder with `python3 -m http.server 8461 --bind 127.0.0.1`, then run `node scripts/browser-check.cjs` in another terminal. The check uses the existing Playwright package at `/tmp/rich-review-05-browser/node_modules/playwright` and system Chrome. Override with `FIELD_PLAYWRIGHT`, `FIELD_CHROME` or `FIELD_URL` if needed. The browser is isolated from the campaign's shared browser session.

# critique-response-59

## Entry point

Open [index.html](index.html), or run:

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/59-critique-response-59/index.html
```

The report and its corrected [compact](baseline-52/compact.html) / [fuller](baseline-52/fuller.html) PR-131 explanations open directly from disk. No installation, server or network is needed.

## Kind

critique — with a repaired comparison pair, operated observations, exact parent/child witnesses and candidate parent additions.

## Subjects

pr-131 — base `b3a6c4fa5dcf96223765aa147a9e094cd4a51b0e` to head `b100221db48754656328391b878299c5a0bab443`.

51 was inspected as the explicitly requested earlier stack artifact. This audit covers all four of its PR-131 author-bullet mappings, relevant policy-table/helper descendants, and all visible fronts as possible alternative parents. It does not audit the other 113 author-bullet mappings or independently review another PR’s implementation. The thirty-proposition crosswalk separately identifies additional PR-131 source coverage and later-stage distinctions.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: Auditor and editor; ask whether a parent supplies the conditions and outcomes needed for a prediction.
- Box lenses: Static package/module dependency and value authority; runtime failure and lifetime boundaries. The copied pair retains separate client-process, daemon-process and worker-thread containment, while the audit follows parent parsing, startup retry, shutdown waits and test construction/capture boundaries.
- Opening style: Before/after of the actual shared arrow error, reduced to one relationship and marked as lossy. CLI imports daemon policy; composition separately supplies values to mechanisms.
- Shape: Complete critique findings, four authored mappings, six table/helper comparisons, a thirty-proposition source crosswalk, then observations and provenance. The two repaired PR pages retain their own complete stopping layers and shared depth.
- Navigation: Continuous reading, findings-to-witness links, native disclosures, original-parent exits, local source lines and return links. The inherited pair retains its exact-focus return enhancement. The report works without JavaScript.
- Trust posture: Include ancestors and other declared fronts before calling something missing. Separate an actual descent surprise from additional source coverage, a weak local attachment, or a later stack stage. Preserve stated versus unexplained reason scope; do not issue a Symnav correctness verdict.
- Persona: A TypeScript-familiar teammate who does not know this daemon area; the copied pair supplies the product/runtime introduction.
- Representations used: Corrected package diptychs, retained runtime map, exact quotation pairs, prediction questions, source-derived cases, a manual crosswalk, browser captures, line-addressable witnesses and an exact repair patch. No simulation is presented as execution.
- Importance rule: Prediction-changing conditions, authority direction and reason scope first. Exact numbers deepen an already named bound; a new failure trigger, budget relationship, state owner or test premise needs a parent. Counts are inventory/provenance aids, not scores.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): Philosophy first and the playbook; selected base/head production, helper and test source and patch regions; policy and architecture plans; pinned `program.ts` context for import direction; git revision/status and source-object comparisons; earlier material listed below. All 123 inherited source snapshots plus two program context snapshots were checked against pinned PR-131 git objects. This is not an independent semantic reread of every line of all sixty changed files. No web research or failed-v1 reading.
- Tech: Offline HTML/CSS; Python standard-library preparation, generation and verification; Node/Playwright with local Chrome for observations. Harness: Codex, no delegated agents and no dependency installation. Browser scripts use the already available `/tmp/rich-review-05-browser/node_modules/playwright` installation; this is only a reproduction dependency, not a reader dependency.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): Read 49-follow-next-49’s PR-131 validation packets, protocol and four retained phase-one accounts; retained excerpts and verified their original seals. Read 51-angle-new-subject-51’s handoff, rendered fronts/descents, authored data and selected frozen helper/policy witnesses. Copied 52-critique-response-52’s pair, kit, ledger, sources and study documents; changed only the shared arrow/caption/accessibility semantics in the reader pages. The kit originally came from 32 and remains unchanged; 32 was not independently reread. Read 54-critique-refresh-50’s critique and browser-harness pattern, and the relevant 51/52 rows of 55-fresh-reader-refresh-50. Other earlier experiments were ignored except their mentions in these records.

## What I tried

Observed the original rendered comparisons before repair. Both 52 static maps pointed policy → CLI while saying “imports / constructs.” Reversed that gray edge in both treatments and both isolated packets, and clarified dependency versus horizontal value supply in the common caption and accessible description. The original experiment remains untouched. [arrow-repair.patch](arrow-repair.patch) records the exact changes.

Then tested the parent relationship at three different scopes: the mapped row, its section ancestor, and the whole declared overview. I withdrew an initial P1 omission claim because the section already says “Required slices replace scattered defaults.” P2’s purpose distinction is available on W3. P9 preserves the two execution budgets. P7 retains test placement and its floor/inert-input warning, while compressing the adapter rationale.

The stronger gaps occur below those mapped author bullets: the table introduces startup-child relaunch, coupled stop/reserve versus independent signal waits, separate sampling jobs, and diagnostic queue/history distinctions. Helper source adds constructor directory creation and the condition/precedence behind legacy-option translation. [Candidate additions](parent-repairs.md) make those relationships explicit. They are concrete editorial proposals, not an applied rewrite or certification of 51’s whole stack.

Compared all thirty 52 propositions with 51’s fronts. Kept additional PR-131 test/API coverage separate from actual authored descendants. Kept 51’s explicit final-stack recovery qualification: it cannot substitute for #131’s terminal failed-fetch path and later-completion-error provenance.

**Observation limit:** I operated pages and inspected source; I was already primed. 49’s four accounts are inherited agent-reader evidence. 52’s unfamiliar-reader trial remains unrun, with its empty slots preserved. I did not fabricate readers, answers, comprehension results or a winning layout. The prepared four questions instead organize clearly attributed author observations.

Validation passed: matching original/repaired registers (thirty propositions, 2,305 words each), sixteen operated descent/return routes across the pair, four viewport widths, no document-level overflow, no page errors or external requests, source jumps, and no-JavaScript reading. The report was also checked at all four widths with every disclosure open. Long identifiers initially overflowed at 320 pixels; wrapping fixed that. Shared overview/depth files are assembly fragments and are validated in their assembled reader page. [verification.json](verification.json), [pair observations](observations/pair-browser.json), [report observations](observations/report-browser.json) and [run-log.md](run-log.md) preserve the checks and harness corrections. A frozen-evidence rebuild reproduced the report byte-for-byte.

To rebuild the report from its retained evidence, run from this folder:

```sh
python3 build.py
```

`python3 prepare.py` recaptures the pair from the named predecessors and pinned worktrees. `python3 verify.py` checks copies, links and tracked worktree state using that original workspace. `observe-originals.mjs`, `observe-pair.mjs` and `check-report.mjs` reproduce the browser work with the local Playwright/Chrome dependency above. None of these is needed to read the delivered artifact.

## What I would drop

The full thirty-row crosswalk is an audit annex; it should not become another required PR reading route. Keeping the full source bank beside both layouts is useful for a portable review, but most readers only need the few witnesses attached to their uncertainty. The stricter diagnostic queue/history parent finding is less decisive than the child-retry and shutdown-budget counterexamples.

## What I would do next

Use the repaired packets with genuinely unfamiliar people under 52’s existing protocol. Separately show 51’s fronts and ask the child-failure and short-stop-budget questions before any table/source descent, then test only those parent additions.

## Time spent

About 30 minutes, including reading, comparison capture, source reconciliation, shared repair, the scoped parent audit, browser checks and handoff. Work stayed in this experiment folder. Both Symnav worktrees retained clean tracked state; no Symnav execution, commit, push, publishing or orchestrator update was performed.

- Built on earlier experiment(s): Read and critique 03-unconstrained-c, 06-hub-and-spokes, 08-adversarial (#148), 12-detective, 18-negative-space, 23-zoom-canvas, 27-test-honesty (#148), 29-refusal, 35-future-self, 49-follow-next-49 (#148 report and four variants), 50-recombine-angles-50. 54-critique-refresh-50 supplies the missing/repeating/promising editorial frame; 55-fresh-reader-refresh-50 supplies the disclosed-reader comparison method and attributed prior route observations. 06/08/49/50 supply substantive source leads, independently checked here. No earlier teaching implementation was copied or edited; exact excerpts are attributed receipts.

## What I tried

Started with ten direct #148 pages. Reading 49's full declarations revealed four documented #148 copies plus its focused report; I added them before sealing rather than silently omitting variants. Full original-copy rendered bodies match 23/29. Each revised opening differs by one statement; selected deeper text remains unchanged. The [variant comparison](receipts/variant-comparison.json) records those checks without claiming a fresh reader result.

Combined the two historical shapes by putting the ledger, learned decisions, source corrections and editorial findings in one visible table. I rejected a separate seven-finding table plus hidden ledger: the first viewport now indexes seven editorial threads, while the full table carries every critique finding. No complete implementation was abandoned.

Checked the ownership counterexample, optional-policy/default boundary, constructor timing, credential branches, standalone-versus-supplied queue clock and changed test stimuli against pinned objects. The policy plan has the same git blob at base and head and states the retirement condition. The source pass also corrected my own imprecise sealed phrase “serial mechanisms”: `fileParallelism:false` serializes daemon test files. That correction stays visible in row 27 rather than rewriting the sealed record.

The optional-policy descent in 29's lower host map (and its copies) is an additional editorial flag beyond 55's selected queue/auth routes. The table identifies that extension. The #131 spill-adapter surprise from prior critiques is deliberately not transferred to 27's #148 row.

Initial canvas capture attempts did not invoke their Playwright expressions, so they stayed at root. A mistyped 27 selector also failed. I fixed the harness and confirmed settled hash routes/screenshots before sealing; [capture adjustments](receipts/capture-adjustments.md) records this. Later artifact checks needed to recognize the canvas's virtual root and wait for scheduled return focus. These were harness corrections, not page-quality findings.

## What I would drop

The repeated original-variant rows add reading length, but their separate documented surfaces make them useful for tracing repairs. I would keep them in this comparison and avoid treating them as independent reader observations. The full source copies could become optional downloads; focused excerpts do most of the explanatory work.

## What I would do next

Promote 23's optional policy/default condition in a separately preserved variant, then ask an unfamiliar human to predict supplied versus omitted policy and token behavior without prompting the disputed terms. Keep this prepared comparison separate from evidence that the trial actually happened.

## Time spent

About 35 minutes wall-clock, beginning around 06:10 UTC on 13 September 2026. Harness: Codex; one agent, no delegation.

## Checks and limitations

[Artifact checks](validation.json) verify the single table, row/recall agreement, exact excerpts, local links, pinned blob/SHA-256 integrity, unchanged captured reading files and source-input hashes. [Browser checks](browser-checks.json) exercise desktop/narrow layouts, transient filters, all fifteen receipt returns, a source-line round trip, print completeness, original entry targets and JavaScript-disabled reading. These checks establish neither exhaustive semantic coverage nor human comprehension.

Both assigned symnav worktrees have no tracked changes. No original artifact, symnav branch, source file or test was edited; no commit, push or external message was made.

Optional regeneration from the retained content and receipts:

```sh
python3 ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/57-recombine-angles-57/tools/build.py
python3 ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/57-recombine-angles-57/tools/verify.py
```

The historical reading captures should not be regenerated in place: their hashes are sealed. `tools/pin-sources.py` requires the original read-only git objects; reading the delivered artifact does not. Browser verification additionally requires the local Playwright installation and Chrome.

# fresh-reader-refresh-50

## Entry point

Open [review.html](review.html). It works directly from disk with no server, install, build, or network.

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/55-fresh-reader-refresh-50/review.html
```

The artifact is **one 53-row comparison table across 43 completed experiments**: decisions learned before the diff, decisions missed or corrected after it, and witnessed rule-4 surprises. All rows are initially visible. Filtering is temporary and stores nothing. [review.md](review.md) is the same table in Markdown; [witnesses.html](witnesses.html) contains 16 pinned receipts with return links.

Nine reading surfaces have witnessed rule-4 surprises, including repeated variants. The five recurring kinds are rationale attribution, optional policy, authentication partition, fixture translation, and queue-clock defaults. This is a bounded observation count, not a completeness score. Several complete #127 registers had no additional consequential miss in the full six-file diff.

## Kind

critique

## Subjects

None assigned as a new teaching page. The critique follows the existing pages' subjects: `pr-127`, `pr-131`, `pr-148`, `stack`, and the adjacent `pr-146`/`pr-147` pair in experiment 30.

The page-only cohort closed on **2026-09-13 at 05:43:01 UTC**, before any input diff was opened. It includes completed teaching/study experiments 01–37, 40, 49–53, their documented variants and the film/starter supplements: [53 routes](routes.json). Both subject tabs in 01 and 20 share their entry row. Critique reports 38/39/41–48, evidence viewers, build templates, abandoned attempts and unfinished 54 were excluded. Later finishes do not retroactively enter the sealed pre-diff pass.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: A reader records what an explanation taught, then compares it with pinned implementation evidence. No implementation-correctness verdict or ranking of pages.
- Box lenses: The reader's complete layer, deeper explanatory layer and source layer. Within findings, distinguish package ownership from process location; input ownership from failure timing; execution from delivery; and test assertions from the states their fixtures reach.
- Opening style: A four-step reading diagram and a concrete prediction problem: naming an owner can still leave a reader unable to predict a result.
- Shape: One comparison table with one row per documented reading surface. Supporting receipts contain exact source/page excerpts, not an additional hidden findings table.
- Navigation: Read every row in order, search temporarily, isolate witnessed rule-4 rows, or follow a finding to its pinned receipt and return. The complete critique is the introduction plus the whole table; the first viewport is an index to that layer.
- Trust posture: Sealed pre-diff recall; pinned base/head git objects; page quotations; source inferences explicitly distinguished from executions. An unremembered first-pass decision is not a claim that the text appears nowhere. “None witnessed” is not a pass certificate.
- Persona: One technically literate agent reading overlapping subjects sequentially. This is not independent unfamiliar-human research.
- Representations used: Reading-sequence diagram, one comparison table, saved rendered text, selected screenshots, optional line-numbered source receipts, hashes and a machine-readable row manifest. A comparison table serves this critique better than another daemon architecture illustration.
- Importance rule: Preserve decisions that change a prediction about ownership, accepted input, failure timing, replay, credentials, retained state, or test stimulus/oracle. Do not turn every additional number or source spelling into a rule-4 surprise. Record declared narrow scope separately from hidden depth.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): `philosophy.md`; playbook §§1, 2, 3, 6, 7; the finished teaching pages and their documented variants; selected explanations on descent; pinned source context from read-only git objects, including the unchanged `plans/005/daemon-policy.md` at #148 base/head. No failed-v1 material, web research, or symnav runtime was used.
- Tech: Static HTML/CSS with a small in-memory filter; Markdown/JSON; Python standard library for receipts/verification; local Playwright/Chromium for browser reading and artifact checks. Existing Playwright availability under `/tmp/rich-review-05-browser` was used as tooling, not as evidence of page quality.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): Read the complete declared layers of all 43 teaching/study experiments in the cohort. Pages 49 and 50 supplied source-informed leads; their findings were independently checked against pinned objects, not credited as new blind discoveries. The initial README metadata scan also exposed critique summaries concerning 04/23/27. No earlier teaching artifact was edited or copied as this critique's implementation.

## What I tried

Read pages in the browser with preformatted source blocks withheld, write recall, inspect selected explanatory descents, then seal the notes and rendered-text captures before opening diffs. [The seal](before-diff-seal.json) records 85 hashes at 05:43:01 UTC; [source capture](source-capture.json) begins at 05:43:56. The learned column condenses [the first recall](notes/01-09-before-diff.md) and [remaining recall](notes/10-53-before-diff.md), which remain unchanged after sealing. Full rendered text sometimes includes off-camera canvas content; this is not an eye-tracking or independent visual-reading experiment. Not every drawer or simulator state was inspected, and film audio was not assessed.

The raw #127 git blobs resolve a conflict between pages: its old five test bodies and helpers are byte-identical. Page 01's “existing call gains await” claim is wrong. The PR body also discloses awaited release, contradicting page 04's “PR body silent” top label and agreeing with that page's own deeper paragraph. The final project graph selects the last configured owner. In #148, the policy plan records when `policy-testing` should retire; “no reason found” needs a narrower claim. These are explanation corrections, not symnav bug verdicts.

The source pass read the full #127 six-file diff; #131 production changes and selected helper/test/policy/benchmark context; #148 changed app/client/clock/registry/routing and test-boundary hunks plus the historical policy plan; selected #146/#147 session/ledger changes; and final-stack ownership/recovery/cwd/test-removal changes. All full pinned patches are saved. I did **not** perform an exhaustive line-by-line semantic audit of the 43,584-line net stack diff or every copied mechanism in #148, and ran no symnav suite, benchmark or malformed-input runtime probe.

I abandoned an “independent fresh reader” interpretation when the metadata scan exposed earlier findings. The page-before-diff sequence remains intact, but the report explicitly treats overlapping reads and donor leads as contamination. I also avoided counting equal variants as independent trials: 23/original23, 29/original29, and the compact/full 52 propositions match in captured rendered text.

Artifact checks are recorded in [verification.json](verification.json): cohort/table coverage, sealed hashes, local links/anchors, Markdown table structure, raw old-test byte comparison, browser opening and filtering. [browser-verification.json](browser-verification.json) also distinguishes the small post-source interaction check of 53 from the sealed reading pass. These checks validate this critique's delivery and provenance, not symnav correctness.

## What I would drop

The ambition to simulate 53 independent fresh readers with one sequential agent. Retain the honest recall/source comparison. Most full-page screenshots are archival overhead; the decisive evidence is a short top/depth quotation pair and the corresponding pinned source. Do not use the number of rows, decisions, or flags as a quality metric.

## What I would do next

Give genuinely unfamiliar readers one page and a few concrete prediction questions before source access. Promote the identified defaults, error boundaries and credential partitions, then repeat those same questions without introducing an unrelated layout change.

## Time spent

About 40 minutes, including the page-only census/readings, source comparisons, table, receipts and verification. No deadline was used. Work stayed inside this experiment; symnav worktrees and earlier experiments were not modified, and no commit or publishing action was performed.

# critique-refresh-50

## Entry point

Open [critique.md](critique.md) in a Markdown viewer. No server is needed.

The [experiment ledger](experiment-ledger.md) covers all 53 finished experiments, 01–53. [Inspection notes](inspection-notes.md) document reading extent, operated routes, source checks, and limitations. The final census at 05:58:55 UTC on 2026-09-13 found no additional finished handoffs; 55 was still unfinished.

## Kind

critique

## Subjects

None assigned. The subjects of this work are the finished experiments. Targeted symnav source reads check their explanatory claims; this is not another PR explanation or a correctness review.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: Editor examining what helps a human understand, what obstructs that, and what evidence supports each claim.
- Box lenses: Static dependencies versus supplied values; runtime ownership and lifetime; public authority and failure boundaries. These distinguish useful representations in the inspected artifacts.
- Opening style: A complete findings table organized as missing, repeating, and promising; linked detail follows.
- Shape: Written critique, per-experiment ledger, and inspection receipts. No page.
- Navigation: Read the critique linearly, jump from its seven findings to their detail, or consult any experiment's ledger row. Supporting documents link back.
- Trust posture: Separate disclosure from rationale, observation from inference, authored models from executed source, and producer results from checks performed here. No global scores or pass/fail certificate.
- Persona: An informed morning editor. This reader has seen earlier critiques and cannot stand in for an unfamiliar human.
- Representations used: Findings and comparison tables, precise parent/child examples, a correction map, browser text captures, selected screenshots, and pinned source witnesses.
- Importance rule: Prioritize false learning, missing conditions or consequences, incorrect reason scope, and repeated reader work. Test changes and small authority choices matter alongside large package moves. Preserve devices that expose different relationships.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): `philosophy.md`; the required playbook sections and relevant evaluation guidance; all 53 root READMEs and delivered artifacts to the extent recorded in the ledger; earlier critiques, reading protocols, kit/runbook contracts, and design notes; read-only pinned Git sources and repository guidance from `worktrees/stack-head`. The supplied `inputs/stack/pr.json` provided #127's body.
- Tech: Markdown; Python for the census, pinned source copies, and link checks; an isolated Playwright context using installed Chrome for local artifact inspection. The existing temporary Playwright installation was reused. No source builds or tests were run.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): Read all finished experiments 01–53, including 50/51/53 as they finished. Used 38/41/43/45/47's critiques and 39/42/44/46/48's reading reports as attributed prior observations; examined the new intervention and transfer evidence in 49/52. Added independent captures, selected operations, and source checks here. Original artifacts remain in their own folders.

## What I tried

Compared the entire finished cohort against the philosophy and hard rules, then pursued concrete disagreements instead of counting agreement among critiques. The resulting seven findings distinguish missing parent consequences, excess reading, reason scope, representation jobs, human context, observation limits, and incomplete correction propagation.

The newer work changes the diagnosis: 49 has bounded fresh-agent intervention evidence; 51 groups the stack around consequences; 52 demonstrates wider-subject kit transfer while leaving its reader trial unrun; 53 adds coupled physical interaction. A new check also found that 52's shared dependency arrow points opposite to its import/construction label.

All 48 inspected HTML entries loaded without page errors under the recorded conditions. The ledger contains exactly 01–53, and local document links were checked. These checks establish access and traceability, not educational effectiveness. Initial browser and locator failures were corrected and are recorded in the inspection notes; no critique approach was abandoned.

## What I would drop

The bulk capture directory is supporting material, not a recommended reading route. The ledger repeats some findings to make individual entries usable; a later handoff could retain only changed claims. Another general essay repeating the existing diagnosis would add little.

## What I would do next

Observe the already prepared comparisons, then audit whether 51's grouped parents preserve their descendants' consequences. Correct 52's shared arrow meaning before using its pair as an explanatory baseline.

## Time spent

About half an hour, including reading, selected browser operations, source checks, writing, and validation.

## Entry point

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/53-be-weird-53/index.html
```

**The release tension bench** explains PR #127 through a spring that resists the reader’s pull. Drag the brass grip, or focus it and use the arrow keys / End. Home lets go. Finish project cleanup or make it throw to free the head handle. The complete explanation is visible above the instrument; no interaction is required to read it.

The folder opens directly without a server, installation, network, or worktree. JavaScript enables the instrument and source dialogs. The complete layer, mechanisms, source book, and their links also work without JavaScript.

## Kind

page

An interactive physical analogy with recordings from actual backend methods and a static evidence book.

## Subjects

pr-127 only — Scope semantic caches to one turn. Base `a1e325a5ff979bdfa25babc5554621c8c0f20497` → head `64919bcbcf7fcc8202779b78c5f069b24662bb18`. Six changed files, +391/−67. No additional PR subjects.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: Learner operating a comparative instrument. Assigned angle: invent a physical or sensory interaction absent from finished experiments; chosen interaction is coupled displacement with nonlinear visual resistance and recoil.
- Box lenses: Static package ownership and runtime object/lifecycle ownership. Core supplies the lifetime class; each TypeScript service owns its own scope instance and six handles. The changed await chain is a separate completion boundary.
- Opening style: A marked spring metaphor, then a before/after ownership diptych. Both versions have emptied their caches while only head remains attached to pending project cleanup.
- Shape: Complete stopping layer with twelve open records, followed by the optional bench, twelve matching mechanisms, and pinned evidence. About 650 words of decisions and reasons; the complete layer spans multiple viewports.
- Navigation: Linear page; ownership box or record → matching mechanism → exact source. Every mechanism returns to its original record. Dialogs restore focus; ordinary anchors, browser history, and a static source book provide fallback navigation.
- Trust posture: Source-grounded explanation with seven stated reasons and five specific rationale gaps. The changed release boundary, projection/API choices, and exact test selection stay visible. No correctness verdict, score, response collection, or persistence.
- Persona: A teammate who knows TypeScript and symnav’s purpose but not this cache implementation.
- Representations used: Elastic pull/recoil, authoritative recorded status readouts, package diptych, object-ownership strip, complete decision records, cache slots, before/after outcome table, lookup/lifecycle flows, public API sketch, test inventory, and numbered source excerpts.
- Importance rule: Put cache clearing and release completion together first; retain every independently meaningful ownership, identity, error, API, and test choice in the open register. No fact is unlocked by pulling harder or completing a sequence.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): Pinned base/head backend and semantic-service source; new core cache and tests; original/added service tests; unchanged core project graph and concrete TypeScript project cleanup; architecture-spec clauses; successful builds in both worktrees; actual-method recording with injected ports; source/hash and original-test comparisons. Bundle inputs used: PR body, six commit records, complete patch, file inventory, and relevant repository/spec material. Other bundles and overview dumps were not used.
- Tech: Plain HTML, CSS, inline SVG, and JavaScript; Python evidence capture/rendering/checking; Node recorder; isolated system Chrome through Playwright. No asset generation service, runtime library, external font, or server. Codex; no delegated agents.

[Survey](novelty-survey.json) and [design notes](design-notes.md) preserve the scope. The forbidden v1 directory was not accessed.

## What I tried

Offered the same hand movement to two return handles. Base moves freely; head stretches toward an asymptote while cleanup is pending and recoils when released. Completing or failing cleanup frees it. The actual promise-state readout remains authoritative even when the illustrative handle is at rest. Displacement represents neither elapsed time nor measured force; this is a visual/motor analogy, not hardware haptics.

Considered friction-driven erasure before implementation, then discarded it: rubbing implies gradual destruction, while this clear is synchronous and caller-held promises can still settle. No full implementation was abandoned halfway. Eight controlled release runs, plus refresh and old-promise recordings, ground the status readouts without claiming a daemon trace.

The audit corrected an excerpt that initially stopped before the new project await, separated test-selection intent from rationale, and verified resize, touch cancellation, and reduced motion. A final survey script accidentally overwrote experiment 52’s README; I restored its exact original 68 lines from its worker transcript and verified the full original Git blob hash. The [restoration receipt](evidence/census-restoration.json) records the repair. No Symnav source was affected.

## What I would drop

The brass finish is expendable. The six single-letter cache slots are also secondary; they need a legend and may add less than the result-identity readout. Full-file source context is useful for auditing but bulky for ordinary reading.

## What I would do next

Give unfamiliar readers this page and an otherwise identical page with resistance disabled. Ask them to predict querying during pending cleanup and receiving a cleanup failure; preserve their explanations without a score or leaderboard.

## Time spent

About 35 minutes, including reading, novelty survey, controlled recordings, implementation, source reconciliation, browser checks, and handoff. No human comprehension trial was performed.

## Evidence and verification

- [Static checks](validation-static.json): all 15 patch hunks assigned to visible records; +391/−67 accounted for; 20 frozen documents checked; 58 source excerpts; local links/anchors; required folder contract; both worktrees have no tracked modifications.
- [Browser checks](validation-browser.json): 13 check groups covering all record returns and source dialogs, keyboard/pointer/touch behavior, four cleanup outcome paths, resizing during a pull, 320/390/768/1440 px layouts, reduced and ordinary motion, printing, and JavaScript-disabled reading. No external requests or browser errors in the final pass. [Screenshots](screenshots/01-opening.png) were visually inspected.
- [Recordings](evidence/observations.json): actual compiled backend/service methods with a fake empty workspace, held project graph, and definition-search observer. Both builds succeeded; recorder assertions passed. The browser only replays the saved observations. The six-slot drawing follows source; occupancy in all six stores was not measured.
- [Test inventory](evidence/inventory.json): five original service cases and all helpers are byte-identical; six service cases and four core cases are added. Existing Symnav test suites were not executed for this experiment. These are source counts, not a test-run claim, and no full command or daemon parity result is asserted.

The cache/release distinction is precise: both versions clear before cleanup; head adds an awaited release barrier and propagates cleanup rejection. The long wait is injected. Concrete TypeScript project cleanup is synchronous, while the graph supports asynchronous project release. The artifact exposes the PR/spec rationale gap without claiming a production correctness defect.

## Regeneration

Opening the page requires none of these commands. With the supplied worktrees still pinned and built, run from this folder:

```sh
python3 capture.py
node record.mjs
python3 build.py
python3 verify.py
```

The recorder checks both pins and clean tracked status before importing the builds. Capture/render/check scripts write only inside this experiment. To repeat browser checks, `browser-check.cjs` uses system Chrome and the existing Playwright package at `/tmp/rich-review-05-browser/node_modules/playwright`; set `BENCH_PLAYWRIGHT` to another installed package path if needed.

The received [brief](brief.md), [design/attempt notes](design-notes.md), original harness logs, and initial browser-check failure receipts are retained. Symnav branches were not modified, committed, pushed, or rebased. Index, queue, and completion handling are left to the orchestrator.


Everything works from files without installation or a server. The hub links the [compact](compact.html) and [fuller](fuller.html) complete layers, [findings](findings.md), [32 transfer record](transfer.md), and [examination of 40](parts-of-40.md).

**The separate unfamiliar-reader trial is unrun.** Two isolated packets and their protocol are prepared; [reader-results.md](reader-results.md) records zero observations. Layout measurements and author inspections are not presented as reader evidence.

## Kind

pair

Also: unchanged-kit transfer, editorial removal analysis, and a prepared reader study with an explicit missing result.

## Subjects

pr-131 — Route daemon thresholds through centralized policy. Base `b3a6c4fa5dcf96223765aa147a9e094cd4a51b0e` → head `b100221db48754656328391b878299c5a0bab443`. Sixty changed files, +1298/−544.

40’s PR 127 artifact was inspected only to examine its explanatory parts, as the assigned angle requires. No additional PR review was produced.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: Learner and editor; explain the consequences a reader needs to carry, then test the cost of presenting them densely.
- Box lenses: Static package/module value authority and runtime client-process/daemon-process/worker-thread topology. The changed authority route is distinct from the retained process and package boundaries.
- Opening style: A marked, lossy three-step value route followed by a package diptych and runtime containment map. It is an orientation; the visible decision register completes the top layer.
- Shape: Two matched pyramids, each with thirty visible propositions, an explicit stopping line, the same two worked cases, before/after mechanisms, and local evidence.
- Navigation: Continuous page, native overview-to-mechanism and source exits, exact return focus with the original kit enhancement, and ordinary fallback links without JavaScript. Reader packets have no crossover links.
- Trust posture: Check earlier claims against the assigned frozen diff and surrounding source. Separate disclosure, reason and consequence. Give test stimulus, fixture casts, adapter precedence, error provenance and reporting changes their own reason scope; no PR correctness verdict.
- Persona: A TypeScript-familiar teammate unfamiliar with this daemon area; a short product/daemon/spool introduction supplies the minimum domain vocabulary.
- Representations used: Package before/after, runtime containment, compact consequence rows versus fuller cards, paired mechanism descriptions, illustrative recovery/storage tables, line-numbered frozen source disclosures, and a research protocol outside the review interface.
- Importance rule: Ownership first, then recovery/timing qualifications, operational consumers, changed test premises, and changed observations/reporting. Preserve every independently meaningful consequence found in the complete diff; never rank by deleting entries. Context qualifications are included where they prevent an overclaim.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): Read philosophy first and playbook in full, with required sections treated as rules; both assigned worktrees’ changed/context source; the unchanged daemon policy implementation/tests and policy/architecture plans; git revision/diff/status checks; the predecessor material named below. Read the bundle PR body/commits, complete patch and file summary; kept the rules compilation as a frozen input and inspected the relevant plans in the worktrees. Did not use overview bundles, the network, or the forbidden v1 directory. No Symnav execution was needed.
- Tech: Python standard library generator/capture/verification; offline HTML/CSS; 32’s original Python/SVG components and navigation JavaScript; Playwright for browser checks. No runtime dependency installation, external assets, persistence, forms or answer collection.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): Read 31-method-runbook’s RUNBOOK and handoff; used its source→decision→parent chain and file-order reread idea, without claiming an unchanged run of its entire line-coverage method. Read and copied 32-kit’s authoring contract and reusable directory; all three kit files remain byte-identical. Read 40-best-of-synthesis’s handoff and operated its rendered page for a part-by-part examination; no recordings or PR-specific prose were imported. Read 47-critique-refresh-40’s critique and relevant 48-fresh-reader-refresh-40 review/recheck findings as correction leads, then checked those against the assigned sources. Other earlier experiments were not directly inspected for this build; mentions inside 40 are attributed to 40’s composition.

## What I tried

Built a corrected shared ledger before presentation. It includes the parent-before-Worker parsing consequence, default versus numeric recovery behavior, terminal failed-fetch path, later-error origin, distinct test-helper effects, unused startup timeout, changed expected-value sources and the benchmark’s extra fields under schemaVersion 1. Split two initially overbroad stated-reason cards: explicit-policy precedence and unknown casts are separately unexplained.

Applied 32’s four components unchanged to the sixty-file subject before adapting anything. The trial generated a complete fuller page but exposed unreadable wide-diagram text on mobile: the 1,100-unit runtime map shrank to 445 pixels and its 13-unit titles to about 5.26 pixels. Preserved that specimen and receipt, then added page-level minimum widths using the existing scroll container. Later visual inspection corrected an authored before-edge label that put local defaults on the composition arrow. No kit file changed.

Then arranged exactly the same root-card DOM as compact rows. This abandons a more ambitious claim about semantic prose compression: the experiment isolates arrangement, not shorter wording. Both registers contain 2,305 rendered words. At 1440 pixels wide, the complete layer ends at 6,291 pixels for compact and 7,781 for fuller. Both remain lengthy on a phone. These are layout observations, not comprehension or time-saving measurements.

Examined 40 by asking what distinct prediction becomes harder if a part disappears. Kept the explanatory jobs of ownership, paired outcomes, separate relationships, scoped rationale and source exits; did not require every donor device to survive. The analysis is explicitly editorial. A browser attempt to advance an already-final cleanup frame timed out on a disabled button; the successful subsequent read and failed call are both preserved. Another initial screenshot failed because its output directory did not yet exist; it was created and the screenshot succeeded.

The request also calls for separate unfamiliar readers. I offered the user a choice of fresh-context agent readers or separate human packets while building; no response arrived before handoff. No agents or humans supplied unfamiliar-reader observations. I prepared two matched, independently assigned entries and a protocol, and recorded the missing result without substituting my primed recall. This portion remains unperformed.

Verification passed: 131 frozen-input/copy hashes, three unchanged kit files, thirty matching propositions, 109 excerpt checks, local links/anchors, twenty operated focus/return paths, deep-source opening and browser Back, four viewport widths for both pages, and reading with JavaScript disabled. [verification.json](verification.json) and [browser-verification.json](browser-verification.json) preserve scope and results. These checks establish artifact integrity, not semantic completeness or Symnav correctness. Both assigned worktrees retained clean tracked status.

From this folder, rebuild with `python3 build.py` and check with `python3 verify.py`. `capture.py` is a read-only recapture tied to the pinned worktrees. `browser-check.js` is a function for the available Playwright tool; it used a temporary localhost server, which is not required to open the delivered pages.

## What I would drop

I would drop any claim that reducing whitespace solves the complete-layer problem, and any “winner” inferred from these geometry measurements. Thirty separate before/after mechanisms produce repetitive scaffolding; keeping their distinct source/return destinations is useful, but they could share more visual structure. 40’s optional depth matrix does not need another counterpart here. The horizontal runtime map is legible after repair but costly to navigate on mobile.

## What I would do next

Run the prepared protocol with two separate unfamiliar readers and preserve literal accounts and descent revisions. Only then test a shorter paraphrase of the same propositions, or remove one optional device from 40, without mixing either intervention into this density comparison.

## Time spent

About 30 minutes, including reading, source reconciliation, unchanged-kit trial, paired rendering, editorial examination, browser checks and handoff. Codex only; no delegated agents.

# angle-new-subject-51

```sh
open ~/projects/rich-review-v2/experiments/51-angle-new-subject-51/index.html
```

An offline page. No install, server or network is needed. All nine fronts, predictions, examples and source disclosures remain readable without JavaScript; JavaScript adds checkpoint selection and exact return positions.

## Kind

page

## Subjects

stack — all 26 PRs, main `b6801ebdd2421d0ca2e4bdd61ec0f04c24ddd73e` to #149 tip `d07002357d3e9596bfaae910a1ac63b77981620b`. Individual PR records and a few intermediate snapshots explain staging within this same subject.

## Declared choices

- Role framing: Learner. Predict one result, step through a small example, inspect the same decision in source.
- Box lenses: Static package ownership and runtime/object lifetimes. The opening distinguishes package movement from the retained CLI-process → daemon-process → worker-thread topology. Each episode then names the state owner and moved boundary.
- Opening style: Three short lifetime intuitions—workspace, accepted request, completion—followed by a runtime map. The intuition and simplified diagrams are marked where they appear.
- Shape: Nine linked small pyramids: host handoff; workspace publication; semantic turns; policy/admission; connection mechanics; transfer recovery; accepted execution/generations; delivery/ACK; final physical ownership. All nine fronts together are the complete overview. The introductory map is explicitly orientation.
- Navigation: Continuous page, a nine-door map, front-to-example exits, prediction disclosures, cross-boundary links, exact scroll/focus returns and line-addressable local source pages. No responses or comments are stored.
- Trust posture: Reconcile the stated preservation promise with actual source boundaries, while keeping disclosure and rationale separate. Surface test stimulus changes, assertion removals, intermediate staging and changes outside a PR’s named purpose. No correctness verdict or inferred author motive.
- Persona: A teammate familiar with symnav but unfamiliar with daemon internals.
- Representations used: Ownership diptychs; runtime topology; nine checkpoint examples; paired main/tip recorded tables; record-offset and queue-gate states; project-owner comparison; predict/reveal prompts; policy table; linked original PR decisions; numbered source excerpts and full source files with net diffs.
- Importance rule: Changed ownership and different lifetimes first; qualifications that change a prediction stay on the same front. Test and unexplained decisions receive the same front visibility. The 117 PR decision bullets map to 59 front consequence rows, rather than becoming a second independent overview. Counts and parent links are an audit aid, not a proof that every implicit choice was found.
- Inputs used (beyond bundle): Read philosophy first and the required playbook sections (also the inspiration menus). Used the supplied stack PR/commit record and file inventory; inspected the overview placeholders but did not use them as semantic evidence. Generated a copy-aware main→tip diff from pinned git objects, inspected selected production/test changes and all changed paths/test-title removals, read the relevant main/tip sources, contributor guide, architecture/policy/follow-up plans, and historical #129/#148 test/retirement context. Ran the controlled source probes described below. Did not read the failed v1 or browse external sources.
- Tech: Native HTML/CSS/JavaScript; Python standard-library generator and verifier; optional Node probes through the prepared worktree’s tsx loader. The probes import real TypeScript source modules; transitive package imports use the prepared workspace dependencies/builds. The shipped artifact contains frozen observations and source and executes no symnav code in the browser. Harness: Codex; no delegated agents.
- Built on earlier experiment(s): Read 04-textbook-chapter, 17-executable-before-after and 40-best-of-synthesis (handoffs and selected page/code content). Reused their prediction, controlled-completion and progressive-depth ideas. Read 47-critique-refresh-40 and 48-fresh-reader-refresh-40 for source/rationale corrections and warnings about surprise on descent. No predecessor implementation or recording was copied. Relevant claims were checked against the pinned source; this experiment’s recordings are new.

## What I tried

Scaled the small-change worked-example pattern by grouping the stack around nine questions a reader can answer independently. Kept source-cache eviction distinct from prepared-index retention; kept semantic reset distinct from backend release completion; kept result fetch distinct from execute reattachment; kept stream completion distinct from ordinary ACK and physical cleanup.

Rejected a second visible inventory of all 117 original PR bullets. Their exact text instead sits beneath the corresponding fronts, with explicit parent links. This keeps author reasons available without making PR chronology the primary explanation. The nine fronts still contain substantial text: the full stack did not become a one-screen change.

The source pass corrected a draft that called existing SHA-256 request hashing new. Only its commandName/request envelope changes. It also separated that request fingerprint from #148’s unrelated compatibility-source digest. A later pass brought #129’s synchronization/oracle test edits onto the host front and moved cross-episode rationale parents onto their own local fronts. No complete approach was abandoned.

The initial ACK probe omitted an observer method required by the real delivery session; fixed the fake collaborator and reran. The browser runner did not expose Node dynamic-import/require APIs, so the check returns its report and the orchestration saves it. These were harness failures, not symnav findings.

The recordings in [evidence/recordings.json](evidence/recordings.json), generated by [probe.mjs](probe.mjs), contain:

| Probe | Real subject code | Controlled part / limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Selection byte eviction, main vs tip | Both WorkspaceSourceCache implementations | Tiny fake filesystem; counts underlying reads, no real disk |
| Prepared-state overlay and rollback | Tip RevisionedBackendState | Tiny language preparation adapter; no ts-morph transaction claim |
| Last configured primary owner | Tip ProjectGraph | Two injected configurations sharing one file |
| Held release, main vs tip | Both TypeScriptBackend implementations and their services | Asynchronous project-release gate; actual TypeScript project cleanup is synchronous |
| Cached undefined and handle reuse | Tip TurnScopedCacheScope | Direct factory inputs; no semantic result parity claim |
| Policy and admission | Tip policy codec/factory and admission guards | 8-GiB memory input and explicit contexts; no process launch |
| Partial frame | Tip DaemonWireCodec | Fragmented in-memory encoded object; no sockets |
| Durable cursor | Tip DaemonResultTransferReceiver | Held append and controlled manifest; no digest finish or disk durability claim |
| Duplicate acceptance | Tip AcceptedRequestLedger | Fixed clock and request |
| FIFO completion gates | Tip AcceptedExecutionSession + WorkspaceRequestQueue + ledger | Immediate fake worker, independent held delivery/sample ports; no real worker or ACK exchange |
| Cleanup failure with successful ACK | Tip DaemonDeliverySession + ledger | Spool cleanup throws; diagnostics/observer are controlled ports |
| Command-looking target | Tip InvocationWorkspaceSelector | `refs def`, help and lifecycle argv; no full CLI execution |

Everything else is explicitly a simplified source trace, including real socket recovery, worker-generation transitions and package-cutover diagrams. This is not a full-stack integration run, benchmark or CI-parity result.

Validation: [verification.json](verification.json) checks local destinations/fragments, 68 source hashes against pinned git objects, the 26-PR/117-decision mapping, selected recording invariants and clean symnav worktree status. [browser-verification.json](browser-verification.json) records 34 checkpoint controls, all 59 exact front return paths, 320/390/768/1440-pixel layouts with all disclosures open, no page errors or external requests, no-JavaScript reading, source fragments and a direct file opening. Four [screenshots](screenshots/01-opening.png) show the opening and selected examples. These checks do not measure reader comprehension.

Rebuild from the frozen evidence, from this folder:

```sh
python3 build.py
python3 verify.py
```

`python3 build.py --capture` additionally reads the original prepared worktrees’ pinned git objects. To rerun the probes, from the repository root:

```sh
node --import ./worktrees/stack-head/apps/cli/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs experiments/51-angle-new-subject-51/probe.mjs
```

[browser-check.js](browser-check.js) is a Playwright-tool function, not a standalone Node script. It expects the artifact served temporarily on `127.0.0.1:5151`; the validation server has been stopped. The artifact itself opens directly from disk.

## What I would drop

The repeated before/after box rows earn less in the transport and final-ownership episodes than the concrete cursor and gate examples. Some could be replaced with a single changed edge. The full policy table belongs behind its disclosure; requiring it in the reading route would make this another long inventory.

## What I would do next

Give an unfamiliar maintainer only the nine fronts, then ask them to predict selection retention, a duplicate accepted request and a held cleanup. Record which first descent changes their account, rather than treating interface checks as evidence that the page taught them.

## Time spent

About 35 minutes, including source reading, new controlled probes, page construction, correction and browser checks.
